13.5 EDITING OF DIFFERENT PROGRAMME FORMATS
Every audio programme format requires editing and it can be done at different levels. Let us study some examples of audio editing and understand it thoroughly.
Editing of Advertisement/Promo
An advertisement or Promo is usually made as a short audio to be effective for promotion of a product/brand/program. They are meant to be very creative and catchy. They usually tend to give more information in a short time period. So, editing should be such. Let us note down some points related to editing of Advertisements/Promos :

* Spaces can be short but not too short for the communication to get mixed up. * Timing is very important. And the sound effects do enhance the impact. e.g. if it is an advertisement for sale the sound effects of crackers or announcement drum etc. can be used. If sfx come even a second later than they are supposed to, you can miss the timing and this will affect and minimize the impact of the advertisement. * Proper equalization, compression is important when needed. Reverb can be used for impactful sound as per the suitability. * No extra word should be kept while editing. * Repetition of program name/brand name can be done as the purpose here is promotion.
Editing of Talk Show
Usually in a talk show, the anchor/RJ talks to one or two guests. It can have a formal or informal approach depending on the subject and purpose. Editing is done after understanding the program content very well. Let us note down some points related to editing of a Talk Show: * Avoid overlapping to the extent possible. * The sound of all the speakers should remain at same levels while listening. * Edit according to the time schedule. Leave the less important points or repetitions. * Make sure that none of the sentences should sound incomplete. * If talk is about a sensitive subject, its sensitivity should be maintained throughout the program. * Do not use too many effects. The original voices should not lose their uniqueness.
Editing of Discussion
Discussions can be hard to edit as more than two people may be present and they may tend to speak cutting each other's point. Let us note down some points related to editing of a Discussion * While minor overlapping is sometimes okay as per the format but excessive chaotic overlapping can result in bad listening experience. In audio program on radio or any other platform, people are solely dependent on the audio and there is a need to maintain clarity as compared to a program with visuals. * When there are multiple people involved, they tend to speak very differently. Some may speak calmly and some furiously. The voice textures, speed of speaking may also differ. Hence the editor has to ensure that one speaker is not overpowering the others on technical grounds. * If while recording the discussion has gone off track, the editor should be able to eliminate those points not connected to the theme of the program.

* Maintaining the balance is also very important. It should not appear as if one speaker is given more space than others. If it is a discussion, everyone's opinion should seem valued in the outcome. * Keep track of time. Sometimes, the flow of discussion may extend beyond the decided time and obviously you cannot play an audio for so long. You should then pick up the best parts and put them together to make a program. However, harmony should be maintained in the content. e.g. one person is talking about his past childhood and we cut directly to when he is talking about his present situation. There should be transitions like 'ok now let me talk about my present' or any other word he said, you can pick from the recorded audio.
Editing of Story
Story is one of the all-time favorite formats as per the audience preference. Editing an audio story is usually a good combination of voice overs, music, and sound effects. Let us note down some important points related to editing of stories : * The storyteller has his/her own flavor which has to be maintained. * Sound effects play a crucial role. If the storyteller is describing about a stormy night, then the sound effect of gusty wind with little scary music can be used as it may help the listener to create a picture in his mind and visualize the scene. However, if you have used the wrong kind of music, the feel of the story could be gone. * Music and effects should not overpower the voice over. * Effects on voice can be used to enhance it. In some cases, base is added to male voices to make it sound good. * The pace of the story should be maintained throughout. Sometimes you not only have to cut but also add spaces to increase the impact of the story.
Editing a Jingle
Jingles have their own composition and they can be very creatively edited. We should keep following points in our mind while editing Jingles : * Editing should ensure that the voice is clear and powerful. When a person sings on microphone his/her breath often gets recorded in between. The sound of breath should be removed as needed. * Instruments which complement the emotion of the jingle should be used. * The rhythm of jingles should remain intact while editing. * Using compressor can ensure that you get the requisite loudness. Jingles are usually short, the voice quality should be distinct. * Try listening from audience point of view and judge the impact.
Editing Drama

Dramas have many elements And they can be very impactful for all kind of audience. Let us note down some points related to editing of Dramas : * Dramas have multiple voices of the character voices which are edited according to the scene and character. For example: A 70 year old woman is angry with her son. So, in this case, her voice may tremble, she may speak her dialogues faster than usual as when people are angry they tend to speak fast unless her character does not allow her to speak fast. So, the spaces can be cut short if the recording has not addressed the specifications. * You should picturize the whole scene in your mind to give it a realistic feel. * While recording sometimes people talk to each other. Eliminate the talk, stick with the script. * People repeat the same dialogue again and again to gain perfection. Choosing the best delivery of dialogue is a big responsibility. Focus on correct pronunciation of words, conveyed emotions and the strength of voice to choose the best option. * Use good sound effects. For example: If there is kitchen scene the sound effects of utensils being washed or put on the slab, something cooking on the gas etc. can be used. Always keep the sound of sfx lower than the dialogues for clarity until the story demands otherwise.
Editing of Teaser
Teasers are meant to create a buzz so editing should solve the purpose. Let us note down some points related to editing of Teasers : * The ending should sound like something is yet to come so such transitions can be used. * To create anticipation, use of heartbeat sound effects (sfx) or time clock ticking etc. can be used as needed. * Timing is the key. It should be short and sound like something interesting is about to come unless it is required to be the other way as per the script.
Editing of Interview
Interviews have detailed insights of a person's life or a subject. Let us note down some points related to editing Interviews : * While recording an Interview, sometimes the guest might go off track with emotions or be very passionate about the subject. Cut the unwanted parts. * You can keep transition music in between two questions as needed. * Be aware and check to see if the guest is not talking anything that can outrage the audience or which is not in accordance with the law. If anything like that is present, be ready to delete it. * Check to see that the name of the guest is correctly pronounced by the anchor, if there has been any mistake in between the interview, please cut the part where he has taken the right

name and paste it in place of the wrong pronunciation. Make sure that the tone and flow of the sentence is not getting disturbed in the process. * Ensure that the edited audio fits into the time slot of the programs. Choose the best parts for the show. * If the guest is taking too many gaps or repeating words like 'mmmm', 'aaaa' or any other word too many times, delete them one by one for a pleasant listening experience.
Editing Children's Program
Children's program should especially be creative to grab the target audience's attention. Let us note down some points related to editing of Children's programmes : * You can use fun music, however, kindly check for the copyrights before using any. * Use funny sound effects .These can be easily found on internet. Also, you can use self- created sound effects. * If there are cartoon characters, you can use 'Change Pitch' effect. The pitch also affects the speed of talking. If you put the value above zero, the voice will be high pitch and going below zero the voice will be low pitch. Depending on the character you can use this effect. For example: A baby bird can have high pitch voice while a policeman can have low pitch cartoonish voice. * If you are editing for a series of program please maintain the editing continuity in character voices and music too. Like the beginning music can be same as well as the ending music. So that audience can identify the program with a piece of music only. * The little sounds made by the characters apart from the dialogues are to be kept as per the need. They help in keeping the program energetic and engaging sometimes. Check Your Progress: 2 Note: 1) Use the space below for you Answers.
2) Compare your Answers with those given at the end of this Unit.
1. What should we keep in mind when editing audio dramas ?

2. List five points to remember while editing children's programme.

13.6 LET US SUM UP
This unit discussed about the various aspects of audio editing. The software helps us to improve the audio but what to do with the tools depends on how much we understand editing in our mind first. We discussed how to edit different formats of audio programs. Editing makes an audio presentable. Practicing the tools of editing, listening to the audio with concentration, observing the details, understanding its need and being creative with it makes us a good editor. Good editing is the backbone of any program.

14.0 INTRODUCTION
Audio editing requires both technical and aesthetic approaches. This job requires an understanding of editing as well as technical knowledge of audio editing software. Audio editing can be done with paid software or open source software which are freely accessible. Every organization which produces audio content usually makes its own choice of software to work with. If you are an individual planning to create your own podcast or learning basic editing, you can download any open source software. A good example of professional open source audio editing software is Audacity. We shall learn about how the software works. Over a period of time, the software often get updated i.e. the version of software changes which may result in certain changes in the look of the software interface or some effects may be added or some processes can be renamed or some processes may be modified. However, if you learn the basics of editing you can find it easy to work on other software as well. In this Unit, we'll discuss the different aspects of audio editing software.
14.1 LEARNING OUTCOMES
After working through this Unit, you will be able to: * discuss the use of audio editing software; * edit an audio file in audio editing software; * apply basic and advanced tools; and * understand the benefits and limitations of editing tools.
14.2 AUDIO EDITING : WORKFLOW

* Import or Record Audio: First, record the audio according to the requirement of the script. If you have already recorded the audio, drag the audio file in the software or import the audio file. Every software has that option mostly in file menu. Common formats used in audio are wav. mp3, MPEG-4 etc. If your recorded audio is not accepted by the audio editing software, convert the audio into one of these formats. Please choose the format which is most suitable for you. Then import the converted audio in the software. Make sure the location of the audio stays the same while you are editing the project. Make a folder, rename it and save all the audios to be used for comfortable editing. * Listen And Make Rough Cuts: Listen to the audio properly and cut the extra audio and vague gaps for primary editing. You can put markers at places where you want to do detailed editing or where you have to select the best from multiple takes. * Edit: Detailed editing is done step -by -step now. Listen to the audio keenly and delete the unwanted words or incorrect audio. Zoom in properly for accurate cuts. Listen attentively to avoid any mistakes. Make sure the audio fits into your desired timeline. * Noise Reduction: It is important to reduce noise for clarity of audio. Noise reduction can be performed by selecting the noise portion of audio and using the 'noise reduction' effect to detect it. Once the software recognizes the noise you can perform noise reduction on the desired audio by selecting it and going to noise reduction effect again. Each audio editing software has this effect but names or way of performing may vary. * Apply Effects: Once you are done with basic editing you can enrich the audio in a creative manner. There are umpteen options under effects dropdown menu for example fade in, pitch shift, compressor etc. You will learn about them in this Unit. * Adjust Volume levels: It is very important to maintain overall volume levels so that the audio will sound consistent. The levels should not be too low or too high to clip. The variations in voice should also be maintained while adjusting volume levels. * Render Final Audio: If editing is not complete, you can save the project. After editing is completed, render the audio in a quality format with proper naming at specific pre- decided location. You can use .wav, mp3 etc. formats.
14.3 THE STRUCTURE OF AN AUDIO EDITING SOFTWARE
As we discussed above, we shall take an open source audio editing software Audacity as our example in this unit. Click on the audacity software icon on your desktop. A window will appear followed by a small box in which the version of the software will be mentioned. Click on 'ok' to proceed. As you enter the software window, you will see a blank space for audio tracks in the center. Toolbars appear above and below the audio track area. There are a few icons which can be identified easily. Some options are listed in the drop-down menu. Let us begin with understanding all the icons and bars available in the software.
Menu Bar

The menu bar is the topmost toolbar. It is shown in the picture below. You will find options like File, Edit, Select, View, Transport, Tracks, Generate, Effect, Analyze, Tools and Help. All these options have drop down menus, where you will find all the requisite actions to perform in order to edit an audio appropriately and creatively. With the help of simple click you can choose the options from the menus. There are short cut keys assigned for each function.
Transport Toolbar
The second one is Transport Toolbar. Here you will find some self-explanatory icons for Pause, Play/Loop Play, Stop, Skip to Start/Select to Start, Skip to End/Select to End and Record/Record New Track. You can see these options in the picture below. Play/Loop Play: The play button will initiate playing the track from the position where the cursor is located. You can move the cursor as per your choice. If you want a certain part of audio track to play in loop, then select the portion and press 'shift+Space'. This information is also visible when you move the mouse over the play button. Stop: This button will stop playing the track as soon as you click on it. If there are multiple tracks on screen, all tracks will be played when you click on 'play' and stop when you click on 'stop'. If you want to perform these actions on a single track, then click on 'solo' on Track Control panel on the left side of the track. Skip to start/Select to Start: This button will bring back the cursor to start of the track irrespective of prior positioning of the cursor. If you want to select the whole portion of audio from start to where your cursor is right now, then you can press 'Shift+Home'. This action can only be performed on the specific track where the cursor is at that moment. Skip to End/Select to End: This button ensures that your cursor moves to end of the audio. To select the track from the position of the cursor to the end press 'Shift+End'. Record/Record New Track: To record audio on a track you can click on record button. As soon as you click on record, it will start recording on the same track which is open. If you want to record audio on a new track, then press 'Shift + R'.
Tools Toolbar
Here you will find tools that are of frequent use. The tools are as follows; please refer to the picture below-

* Selection Tool: You can select the audio or a part of audio on the audio track. Click left button of your mouse and drag to select the part of audio you want. The audio selection will appear gray. * Envelop Tool: This tool assists to reduce the volume of selected portion of your audio on the track. When you select this tool and click on the track, it will create small nodes to alter the amplitude i.e. you can increase or decrease volume. You can move the nodes up or down as per the need. If you click again, it will create more nodes and you can alter the amplitude in greater detail. * Draw Tool: The draw tool allows you to make difference to each sample separately. It helps to repair the frequencies or deal with noise at a very minute level. Keep pressing the left button on mouse and drag the nodules up or down. This tool is used in advance level editing because of its efficiency. If your track is fit into the screen, it will not work. To use the tool, you have to zoom in the audio track till individual modules are visible. * Zoom Tool: This tool will help you zoom in the audio so that you can edit any audio accurately. You can locate and later omit any fumbled word, incorrect sentence, sound of breath or dead gaps etc. When you zoom in and edit them, you make sure that the editing is seamless. If not done so, then sometimes it happens that we mistakenly cut little portion of another word or eliminate gaps too much. The final audio might sound unnatural or half pronounced words may remain in the final output. Editor must see the sound waves as well as listen to the audio with full attention. * Time-Shift Tool: The tools help to move an audio track left, right, up and down in the workspace. Mono audio track can only be dragged to mono tracks and stereo track can only be dragged to stereo tracks. This tool is more useful when working with two or more audio tracks. * Multi Tool: This tool is basically the combination of all 5 tools explained above. It gets changed according to the location or way you use it. Example: If you right click on mouse, it will zoom out and the icon of zoom will appear as you do it. If you click left on mouse the zoom in function will take place. If you bring cursor to middle of the track, selection tool will appear and as you move the cursor on the gray lines, the envelop tool will get activated.
Meter Toolbar
This toolbar assists to monitor the levels of sound being recorded and played. There are two options available in this toolbar-
1. Recording Meter Toolbar: As soon you start speaking on microphone or recording audio in
the software, the recording meter starts showing the volume levels .While recording you can judge if the levels are low, high, or appropriate. You can also click on 'microphone icon' near recording meter and click on 'start monitoring' option. The green color in the meter signifies levels upto-12 dB, yellow color signifies that signal is approaching -6 dB , it moves toward

orange when it goes below that and finally the red color in the meter warns that the signal is approaching 0 dB. In such case the sound gets clipped off and few details of audio get lost. You can drag this toolbar with mouse anywhere on the interface and also adjust its orientation from horizontal to vertical format.
2. Playback Meter Toolbar: The meter displays the sound levels when you play the audio track.
Mixer Toolbar
Here you can increase or decrease volume levels of recording and audio playback. The microphone icon represents the recording audio volume while the speaker icon represents listening audio volume.
Edit Toolbar
Edit toolbar performs the basic functions of editing. The first tool is 'Cut', scissors icon represents it. When you want cut a specific part or divide the audio in sections you can use this tool. The cuts, however, have to be precise or it would sound incomplete. Select the part you want to cut with the help of selection tool and click on 'cut'. You can also use Cltr+X for performing the same action. The next tool is 'copy' which copies the selected audio without removing it from the track. After that there is icon for 'paste' which pastes the selected audio at the position of cursor. Next important option available is 'Trim Audio' that deletes all audio except the selected audio. The next option is 'silence audio' that replaces the selected audio with just silence. Then there are other tools like undo, redo, Zoom in, Zoom out , 'Zoom to selection' that zooms selected part to fit into the track area of screen, 'Fit to Width' which allows the entire audio visible on the track for a overall viewing and last option available is 'Zoom Toggle' to zoom between two preset levels. Refer to the picture below-
Play at Speed Toolbar
This toolbar has option playing the audio with increased or decreased speed. If you have edited an audio and you want to recheck but got less time to do it, sometimes playing the audio in increased speed helps. But it is suggested that you recheck the audio at normal speed to get an overview of actual deliverable content. If you want to check the song lyrics or a few words pronunciation accurately you can review it by slowing down the speed. You can also resize the

bar as you like. The play button is right behind '-' sign. If you have increased the speed and clicked the normal play button at the Transport play bar, it will play normally with no changes in speed. For the changes you want in speed you have to click on the play button of this toolbar only. You can increase or decrease the speed with the help of left click on mouse.
Device Toolbar
Device toolbar shows you the devices that are selected for recording and playback for the audio in the software. You can change the selection of these devices through this toolbar only. You can see and change the microphone, speaker, audio host, and recording channel to mono or stereo.
Selection Toolbar
This toolbar is placed at the bottom of the window. You can see and change the project rate, snap to and choose the kind of timer you want to see. The project rate is basically the sample rate of the current project you are working on. Mostly by default option 44100 Hz is there. You can choose 48000 Hz sample rate for better clarity but as you increase the rate the file size will also increase. Example: If you import a track recorded on 44100 Hz but you have set the project rate at 48000 Hz, The playback of the same audio will be at 48000 Hz and all the new recordings will be on 48000 Hz only. When it comes to the timer you have seen in this toolbar, there are multiple options available to you. You can select from the drop down menu whether you want to see Start and End of the selection, Start and length of the selection, Length and end of the selection or Length and center of the selection. Whatever you choose it will be visible in timing section below. You can change the format of timing visibility by a right click on the timing visible or clicking on the triangle at its corner. You can check other formats from the menu like file frames (24 fpc), NTSC frames etc. Refer to the picture below.
Time Toolbar
It is the toolbar adjacent to Selection Toolbar. It tells the exact time where cursor is on the track at that moment. The format by default is set to hh:mm:ss, which means Hours:Minutes:Seconds. You can change this by right clicking on the bar or clicking the little arrow on the bar. A menu will appear as you do that. Now you can change the format to seconds, Days:Hours:Minutes:Seconds, Samples, HH:MM:SS + Film frames etc.
Status Bar
It is the lowest bar in the software that shows which action or function is being performed on the software. When you are recording it will show 'recording' and when you are playing the audio it

will show 'Playing' and so on. Also in the extreme right corner is the sample rate of the recording. Check Your Progress: 1 Note: 1) Use the space below for you Answers.

14.4 AUDIO TRACK
The audio track is the space where you record or edit the audio. When you want to edit an audio file you can do it by going to File menu and selecting Import then Audio. You can also drag the audio into the audio track. If you have already been working on an audio, it might be visible in recent files under File Menu, you can select the audio from there. The audio is visible is a wave form of purple color in Audacity software window. The audio can be anything from a 1 second clip to hours of recorded session. It can be recorded audio from a mobile phone or high end recording from a microphone in studio. You can see the peaks and understand how much loudness it carries and what its average recording range is. You can zoom in to have a better view of track by pressing control key and rolling the mouse.
14.5 TIME LINE
The time line is the line right above the audio track. The exact length of audio in hours, minutes and seconds is visible above the audio. If we zoom in the time line, it will show audio divided in milliseconds. It is very important to know the exact time of audio while working on it. The

edited audio has to fit into a specific time schedule. For example, if you are making 40 seconds advertisement for a radio channel, you have to be very specific with the time. Advertisements have cost attached per second. Same goes with any other program even if cost is not attached; the slot of broadcast has a fixed time schedule. It also helps to identify where a specific overlapping or recording error is present. You can inform the concerned person if there is a need to re-record a specific part. You can right click on the timeline and enable quick play, dragging selection, while playing. You can also select 'pinned play head' so that starting of the audio will be pinned on screen. Generally, the audio is not pinned while editing. You can see what the timeline looks like in the picture below-
14.6 TRACK CONTROL PANEL
Track Control Panel is placed at left side of the audio tracks. There is a drop down menu which will appear when we click on the arrow beside Audio Track. You can rename the track; move the tracks up and down while working in multi-track. You can change the color of the waveform to make working on multi track easy and more enjoyable. You can also split the stereo track and make stereo track too. Apart from the drop down menu, there is an option to increase and decrease volume levels of the track. You may pan the audio from left to right channel or vice versa. If you are working on more than two tracks, sometimes you have to listen to one track and sometimes to the other. In such cases, to make it easy, you can mute one track to hear other tracks. If you want to mute all other tracks and listen to a specific track then click on 'solo' option on its track control menu so that only that track will be played. At the bottom of the panel 'select' is written, if you click on it, the entire track will get selected. The selection is necessary for applying any effect on track. Refer to the picture below for getting an overview.

14.7 MENUS IN MENU BAR
Let us understand different menus of Menu bar. File: As shown in the below picture, file menu provides you with basic options of any software. Example- 'New' for opening a new project.'Open' for opening an already existing project of same software. 'Recent Files' for opening an audio file you were editing recently. 'Import' for importing any audio file. If the software is not accepting your audio file, you may convert it to WAV, MP3, AIFF,OGG, etc. 'Export' for saving the final outcome in an audio format. 'Save Project' for saving the entire project when you still have to work in the same project file later. Refer to the picture below- Edit: This menu gives you options to make certain changes in track. Example- Undo, Redo, Cut, Copy, Delete, Paste are the basic functions. There are other options also available like 'Duplicate' which duplicates the selected portion of the track to another track. 'Remove Special' has further more options available like split cut, split delete, silence audio and trim audio. 'Split cut' will cut the selection part of the track and divide the audio into two parts. 'Split delete' deletes the entire selected portion of the track and divide the audio into two parts. If you select 'silence audio' then the selected part of the audio will be completely silenced. Trim audio lets the selected portion of the audio to remain and deletes the rest of the track. You can see the options in the picture below. Select: This menu lets you make selections in the tracks of a particular project. "All' lets you select all the tracks present in the project. 'None' lets you deselect all the selections made. 'Tracks' this option is effective when you are working on more than a single track. You can make the selection of a particular section on all the tracks at the same time by using this; it brings the cursor to all the tracks on same position at the time line. 'Region' lets you select the exact region of audio you want. The select menu is shown in the below picture.

View: This menu gives multiple options. 'Zoom' to zoom in or zoom out the track. 'Track size' has sub options like 'Fit to width' to make all the tracks visible fully in the software, 'Fit to height' to Resize the height of tracks so that all the tracks are equally visible on the screen at the same time, 'Collapse all track' makes all the tracks collapse into the screen and 'Expand Collapsed tracks' lets the collapsed track expand again. There are other options available like 'Skip to' to skip the cursor at the start or end of the track. 'History' option lets you see the earlier changes you have made on tracks. 'Mixer Board' which lets the mixer board placed at the left corner of each track visible separately on screen. 'Toolbar' option allows you to make all other toolbars visible or not visible. If by any chance any toolbar is not showing in the software, you can tick on its name in this option and it will be visible again. Refer to the below picture for software view of this menu. Transport: This menu helps to control the playing and recording options. You can Play, Stop, play in loop by selecting the first option 'Playing' in the menu. You can record, stop or pause etc. under the second option of 'Recording'. Shifting the position of cursor, deciding the play region is possible under this menu. The Transport menu is shown in the below picture.

Tracks: In this menu, you will find multiple options related to functioning of audio tracks. By selecting 'Add New' from the menu you can add multiple Mono or stereo tracks in the current project. 'Mix' option has a sub menu in which 'mix stereo down to mono' option allows mixing stereo tracks to mono. 'Mix and Render' option takes all the tracks present in a project and makes it into one track. 'Mix and Render to new track' is an option that allows the software to mix all the tracks and place the final output on a new track. Under Track Menu other options allow you to resample the tracks, remove tracks, mute, unmute tracks, align tracks etc. Refer to the picture below- Generate: As you can see in the below picture, this menu helps in generating certain sounds like Chirp, DTMF tones, Noise etc. Effects: There are multiple effects which can make an audio effective. While audio effects enhance audio presentation and listening experience, they can make the audio sound ineffective if not chosen wisely or if over used. So once you begin to use these effects, be attentive to the changes they are making to the sound of audio and its waveform .See the picture below which shows some options available under this menu.

Noise Reduction: When we record an audio, it can be indoor recording or outdoor recording. Both can contain different kinds of noise. Even when we record inside a closed room or studio, noise can be present e.g. Computer or any other machine's noise, AC or fan noise .In outdoor settings, there can be many unwanted sounds which are considered as noise e.g. while recording in the roadside, the noise of vehicles, birds chirping, other ambient noise etc. To reduce such noises, noise reduction is performed. Different software have their own presentation for the same e.g. if you are working in Audacity you first have to select only the noise portion with the help of select tool, then you can go to 'Effects' and click on 'Noise Reduction" and select "Get Noise Profile". This step helps the software to identify the kind of noise that is present in the audio file. Now as you want to remove noise from the whole file, select the whole file and then again go to 'effects' and select' noise reduction'. There will appear a box with three options. You can use the preset values for initial understanding. Then you can learn by trying out how many decibels you want to reduce the noise, how much harsh or sensitive you want the software to be with noise and to what extent the frequency curves of noise are to be smoothened. Below there are two check boxes i.e. 'Reduce' or 'Residue'. You should choose 'Reduce' so that the noise profile identified by the software will reduce that noise only from the whole audio. If you want to separately hear the noise or keep the noise for any purpose, you choose 'Residue' and click on Ok. You will find all other audio frequencies gone expect the noise.
Points to Remember
* Leave recording on without speaking anything, so that while on the editing table you can easily select noise present in the audio for noise reduction. * Carefully select the noise area. If you select the breathing or speech part even a little the noise reduction can eliminate the required audio frequencies. * While doing the process, keep in mind that the audio should not sound unnatural. * Try using 'preview' option before applying the noise reduction on whole audio to get a proper understanding of how much noise is being removed. * Even after the noise removal if there is some ambient noise left in outdoor recording, don't flatten the frequency curves of gaps between the words or else it might feel like jerks in between the words/sentences while listening. * If you want to repeat the same process, you can simply go to 'effects' and click on 'Repeat' or use the shortcut key CLT+R.

* Don't over use the effect or else the voice texture may lose its quality. * If noise is present in some parts of the audio then deal with it in parts, do not use noise reduction on the whole audio. * If you have done an outdoor recording, depending on the requirement you can keep some of ambience sound to make it sound more realistic. E.g. If you are broadcasting an outdoor discussion program recorded in a village and the audio plays without any ambience sound, the audience might get confused as it sounds like people are sitting inside a room and talking to each other. Though the ambience should not overpower the speech, you have to listen properly to make a good decision about how much you want to reduce the noise while editing. Limitations: * It is nearly impossible to separate two overlapping voices of people. * If the noise is more than the speech, the quality of audio after noise reduction might decrease. Auto Duck: This tool is useful when you are working on more than one track. When you want to add music behind the voice over then put music on the first track and voice over below that track. Select music and click on Auto duck. It will automatically reduce the levels of music when voice over is there and increase when Voice over is not there i.e. before and after portions of the voice over, music will be loud. The level of Voice should be more, and level of music should be low. By listening carefully, you have to decide if the levels of music are complementing the Voice and not overpowering it. Repeat: Select the parts of the audio you want to repeat and click on this effect. The same part will get repeated. You can also choose number of times the repetition should take place. Reverb: Reverb is an effect of sound when it hits a hard surface and bounces back to the ears. With the help of this effect you can create a feel of big concert hall or a small intimate space as you need. You can increase or decrease the room size. You can decide the percentage of reverb, pre-delay, wet gain, dry gain etc. Before going too deep, start practicing with the room size and percentage of reverb. There are some factory presets available under the 'Manage' option. Echo: Echo is the sound that reaches the ear after a delay due to reflection from a surface. Echo depends on how much distant the surface is present. Imagine you standing on a mountain top and speaking anything. Your sound will get reflected from other mountains and will come back to you with a delay and less volume levels. You can get the same result by using this effect. Sometimes advertisements on audio platform or announcements done on speakers in the city/village use this effect. Crossfade Tracks: This is a transition effect. When you have two adjacent audios and you do not want gap between two audio tracks or the second audio to start suddenly, use this effect. This will allow the first audio track to fade out and the second audio track to fade into each other. High Pass Filter: It is also called Low Cut Filter. You set up a bar above which all the frequencies will pass and below which all the frequencies will be cut down. This is a very effective tool. For using this filter efficiently, it will be good if you learn recognizing the

frequencies. e.g. Male voices have more base, female voices have higher frequencies. Drum is a low frequency instrument while flute is high frequency instrument. Low Pass Filter: It is also called High cut filter as it cut down the higher frequencies than the set bar. For example somebody has recorded drum and the rim of a drum is loose. During that process, some unwanted sound of rim also got recorded with it. Both sounds are merged in one waveform. You may enter the value 200 in this filter. If drum sound is low frequency and rim sound is higher frequency, this filter will cut the frequencies higher than 200 dB. Limiter: The limiter prevents your audio to clip. When the audio reaches above 0 dB it clips. The sound it produces is very unclear and loud. You never want that to remain in your audio. When one person is speaking or singing certain words come out loud while others are soft and mellow. When you amplify the whole audio for a better experience, the louder parts may reach above 0 dB frequencies. To avoid this, Limiter is used. Select the audio and click on 'Limiter' then you may put -1 dB value, leaving little headroom for frequencies. It will not let any frequency throughout the selected audio to clip. Fade In: When any audio starts, you do not want it to start suddenly until it is the requirement of the content or it is done for a creative purpose. Fade In option allows the audio to gradually increase the volume levels in the starting. Fade Out: This effect allows the end of the audio to slowly decrease the volume levels. Some scheduling software in Radio Stations have already setup Fade Out option which fades out each audio after being played. In such case there is no need to use this effect in editing. Filter Curve: It is a very effective equalization tool. It helps to make changes to the frequencies. You can enhance or cut down as per the audio requirement. As you select the audio and click on Filter Curve effect, you will find a graph in front of you. The horizontal line represents frequencies we hear from 20 Hz to 20,000 Hz divided into low, mid and high frequency levels. The vertical line represents how much we want to increase or decrease the frequency levels in dB, ranging from 30 dB to -30dB. The green line curve represents the changes you make. If you want to cut down treble i.e. the high frequencies above 10,000 Hz, you can do it manually. Click on the green line right above 10,000 Hz, a small white dot will appear. You can move that dot by clicking left button on the mouse. By moving the dot, you can increase or decrease frequencies in decibels. You may create many such dots and if you want to remove any dot simply drag it outside the box. There are certain presets also available. Click on 'Manage' then 'Factory Presets', you will find options like AM Radio, Bass cut etc. You can try these and check out the impact. Click on the 'Preview' to listen to the impact before making changes on the audio. If you want to see what changes it makes on the waveform, you have to apply the effect by clicking ok. You can undo it later by clicking on the undo icon or shortcut key Ctrl + Z. You can also modify the factory presets. You can select 'Flatten Curve' if you want to undo all the changes. For example: a recorded female voice has some bass vehicle noise. You can cut a little bass to provide strength to the audio. Graphic EQ: This effect also allows you to manipulate frequencies but it has a different style of doing it. You can boost or cut down certain frequencies. You can increase or decrease the

frequency between 20 Hz to 20,000 Hz. It has Factory presets under the option of 'Manage'. Factory presets are default settings made available to you by the software. Normalize: It allows you to set the peaks of audio at a certain level. It manages the parts of audio if they are low or whole audio levels if required. Sometimes even the noise gets enhanced in this process. You can use Noise removal first to use this effect. You can set the peak amplitude level maximum up to 0 dB as it would not accept any value above that. Reverse: Reverse of the word 'SOUND' is 'DNUOS'. This is what the reverse effect does to the audio. It makes the selected portion just the reverse of it. If you choose this effect, you can also see the changes it makes in the waveform of audio. Compressor: It is a very useful tool to manage the dynamic range. It takes the loudest portions of the audio and makes it softer. The dynamic range i.e. the range between the loudest and the lowest frequencies is adjusted to create a warm and smooth experience of listening. There is a lot for you to explore in this tool. Threshold decides above what audio level compression will be done. The Noise Floor option prevents amplification of background level, so that the unwanted frequencies do not get affected. This is mainly useful when compressing speech, to prevent the gain increasing during pauses and so over-amplifying the background noise. Ratio decides how much compression will be done to the audio above the threshold level you have decided earlier. As the name suggests 'Attack Time' is responsible for how fast or slowly the compressor will start working on levels above the threshold. Release Time decides how soon the compressor will start to release the volume level back to normal after the volume level goes below the threshold. High ratio means the impact or compression will be sudden as compared to low ratio. You can try different combinations to get a better understanding. The 'Preview' option is available to listen to the changes before they are applied to the audio. You can tick the option 'Make up gain' so that the audio does not lose its volume level in the process of compression.
16.7.9 Analyze: In this menu you have options like 'Plot Spectrum' which is a complete
frequency analysis present in graphical form. You can add plugins as this menu also provides options for labeling the sounds, finding clipping etc. Tools: This menu allows you to make certain technical changes in the software. For example- Reset configuration, Macros, Run Benchmark etc. You can also take screen shot with the help of Tools menu. You can identify the options in the picture below-

Extras: This menu will help you deal with other menu options separately. You have some extra commands for track focus etc. available here. You can also assign shortcuts with the help of this menu. This menu can be turned on/off by going to view menu and clicking on Extra Menu on/off.
14.8 LET US SUM UP
We tried to learn about working on an audio editing software. We worked through all the menu bar options and tools of the software and learnt about their functions in depth. We understood the division of frequencies and how increasing or decreasing them affects the audio. We also learnt about role of Audio Tracks, Audio Track Panel and Timeline. We also looked into minute details of editing. We discussed the use of various effects on audio like Noise Reduction, Auto Duck, Normalize, Graphic EQ, Compressor etc. We discussed about how overusing the effects can hamper the quality of audio. We learnt that the audio after editing should sound natural unless it is meant to sound robotic or distorted for a reason.

2.0 INTRODUCTION
All audio programs go through almost the same process of production irrespective of the platform through which they are being delivered. Producing informative, entertaining and educative programmes that are effective for the target audience, would be the aim of any producer. The popularity of a podcast channel depends upon the quality and content of its programmes. Every programme needs to go through a planning and preparation stage before it gets produced. In this unit we will discuss various stages of programme production and you will be able to appreciate that how much effort and thinking is required to make it effective and popular.
2.1 LEARNING OUTCOMES
After studying this unit, you will be able to: * discuss the different production stages of an audio programme; * understand the requirements of various stages in Programme Production; and * describe the specific planning required for programmes of special nature.
2.2 PROGRAMME PRODUCTION : DIFFERENT STAGES

There are three stages in programme production process, i.e., preproduction, production and post-production. While planning is required at every stage, extensive planning is required at the Pre-Production stage when the programme is conceived and all the necessary preparations are made. Without proper planning, any interesting theme or creative idea may not make the desired impact. In the Production stage actual recording takes place after doing proper rehearsals. There could be more than one take of any piece of recording due to various reasons. The best take is chosen at the time of editing which is a part of Post Production. In post-production many other inputs are given for the value addition of any programme. Adding sound effects and making a final master copy of any programme (Mixed Master) in also undertaken during post production process.
2.3 PLANNING AN AUDIO PROGRAMME
Planning, as you are aware, is crucial for any activity, whether it is audio programming or nation-building. But, before planning an audio programme, you must constantly keep in mind the strengths and limitations of the medium. Thus, communication over audio podcast or radio depends on the message transmitted through sound to a listener, who has to first listen and then interpret it to grasp the message. Not only the verbal expression of the communicator, but also the listening and understanding capacity of the listener is involved in an effective communication. To achieve this, the message has to be designed carefully. To know that the effective communication is achieved, proper audience feedback is necessary. It is essential to remember that a programme on audio platforms is addressed to 'a' listener. It is a 'one-to-one' communication though several people who are listening to the same programme also get this communications simultaneously. We have no reason to believe that a dull and boring programme, even if informative, will be listened to. Programme should be planned and executed in such a manner that it attracts and holds the attention of the listener.
2.3.1 Pre-requisites of an Audio Programme
Planning a programme requires an understanding of the requisites of the medium. The theme and style of a programme should be capable of exploiting the potential of the medium. It must be suitable for the target audience. An effective programme will have the following attributes: Interest: The first attribute of a programme is that it should be interesting both in terms of content and presentation. The voice quality must be such that can captivate listeners. For example, if drama is not well acted, script is badly read, then you cannot expect the listener to be interested. A poor performance kills the interest. Relevance: It relates to the lives of listeners in some way so that they Production Process feel involved. It may concern their livelihood, their environment or just about their activity and emotions. It may, arouse admiration, curiosity, or show individuals in unusual places. Facts are generally dull, but people are interesting. Comprehension: In addition to being relevant and interesting, the programme needs to be comprehensible to audience. The listeners should be able to understand the content to derive

benefit from it. It should also try to create concrete images avoiding abstract ideas as complexity leads to confusion. Conflict: The element of conflict stimulates interest, whether it is between people, nations, ideas or with nature. It may bring out a controversy, a contrast or a clash of some sort. It may be in the form of a struggle, or a problem or even a challenging question. The ultimate goal of any good audio programme is to disseminate appropriate information on a relevant theme. The planning efforts must be directed towards this goal so that the message conveyed produces the desired impact.
2.3.2 Elements of an Audio Programme
Audio programmes are made up of speech, sound effects, music and pause. A programmer has to plan a judicious use of all of the four elements, which are described below: Spoken-word : It is a very powerful tool of communication among people sharing a common language. Speech is made up of words and, therefore, spoken-word is the most common and most important element of the majority of audio programmes. A audio programmer paints pictures or makes images through these words. Words present the content of the programme and voice renders them meaningful. Sound effects: Sounds are universal in nature and can be understood by all linguistic groups. For example, sounds of wind, water flowing, storm, chirping birds, speeding motor car, gunshot, bomb blast, laughing, crying, etc., all fall under this category. These sounds can be recorded naturally or can be artificially created in the studio. When used in an audio programme, these are called 'sound effects.' Sound effects not only create an environment of the locale, but also project the image of the character. Some sounds are indicators of some happenings or events such as a knock on the door or a call bell which indicate that somebody has come to visit. Sound of a bird chirping indicates that it is dawn. Likewise, the sound of an owl or cockroaches is indicative of night time. There are also special sounds, such as echoed voices of the supernatural, the distorted voice of a puppet or a ghost or the roar of a lion, the chirping of a bird or a robot speech in a metallic tone. Music: There are several forms of music on any audio platform such as film music, light music, folk music, classical music or western music. Music can be used to produce programmes like features or operas. Music is also used as a sound effect in many programmes to create the environment or mood. That's why in stocked tapes of music, a piece can be termed as a happy music, sad music or party music. We may use special music in the scenes of storm, war, march- past or death. Pause: In a medium of sound, pauses have a role to play. Pauses are used imaginatively to convey meaning. You may ask, how a silence or pause can communicate. Yes, it can and that too very powerfully. Let us take an example. A mother on her death bed speaks to her son and suddenly her voice stops. Son provokes "Speak up mother, speak up". But, there is a silence. Here, pause or silence conveys the fear of death, helplessness and a lot of other feelings and emotions attached to it.
2.3.3 Target Planning

It is imperative before undertaking any audio programme you must have a clear idea about your target audiences-their age, their educational and economic status, their likes/dislikes, their level of comprehension, etc. For example, if it is a programme for women, then you must know whether they are urban or rural. If they are urban, whether they are homemakers or working women. You must keep in your mind what subjects would interest them, what is relevant to them and what they will do with it. This information serves as an important backdrop in deciding the content, style, format and pace of the programme. To make the programme material more relevant and useful, you have to pitch it at the right level and for that you require to know about the audiences. Generally, audience for any common programme is a very heterogeneous group, especially in our country, which is so vast and diverse. You may have to cater to an audience, which is culturally, socially, regionally or linguistically quite heterogeneous. While looking at the composition of your audience, you will also have to analyse their needs. You have to access their aspirations by providing them with an appropriate programme. You need to keep in mind the principle of demand and supply, and produce the right kind of product which is in demand. However, like all the other mass media, audio platforms also have a dual role to play, providing the listeners with what they want along with items which they need, i.e., reflect the opinion of masses and also shape or modify the opinion. Hence, sometimes you need to supply a different kind of product looking at the larger interest of the society or nation. In that case, you need to design your programme in such a way so as to create its demand. Activity 1 Listen to one news and one story based audio podcast. Analyse the use of various elements of audio programmes in them. In this context, compare news and story podcasts and write the differences between them. 2) Compare your answers with those given at the end of this unit.
1. What are the elements of an Audio Program ?

2.4 PRE PRODUCTION : DIFFERENT ACTIVITIES
There are some common elements in planning audio programmes in different formats though the methodology of planning certain programmes may vary. Let us have a look at some of these common elements. Identifying the Aim and Defining the Scope : In planning an effective audio programme, the most important step is to identify the broad aim of the programme - whether the intended programme imparts education, whether it is informative, aimed to generate awareness or enrichment type or entertaining in nature. Working out objectives of an audio programme in

clear-cut terms is an important part of the planning process because your entire effort is geared towards achieving those objectives. When a decision is taken on producing a programme on a particular subject, the next stage is conceptualization. The producer has to draw an outline of the programme indicating the main focus and other aspects that need projection. The scope is the framework on which planning is organized. It reflects the need assessment of the programme and production requirements. Content Planning and Research : Content planning begins when you collect and collate all the material connected with a subject. Selecting the right material help in content planning which must ensure that the programme does full justice to the subject chosen. Overload of information may mar a programme. If the subject is vast, you may plan a series of programmes to do full justice to the topic instead of cramming all information in a single programme. If the producer has to prepare a programme on child labour, for example, s/he has to study the subject including legal, social, anthropological and other aspects and consult a number of experts in the area. If the subject is complex or technical, the producer has to engage an expert to provide research inputs. Selection of Format : The word 'format' is used to refer to the form of the programme such as the talk format, the story format, the feature format and so on. Scripts can be written in many basic formats such as news bulletin, feature or documentary. The selection of format depends not on the novelty of the format, but on its suitability to express a given idea to a given audience. These formats can be used individually or in combination to make audio programmes interesting and absorbing. Many of the formats get their names from their usage in literature, e.g., story, drama; but nomenclatures, such as feature and documentary have their origin elsewhere. Selection of Scriptwriter and Other Talents : In audio programmes, the producer may write the script himself or engages a scriptwriter. The selection of a script writer is of crucial importance. The producer has to brief the scriptwriter on the scope of the programme and ensure that the script meets the requirements of the programme. If the producer gets a good script, half the 'battle' of making a good programme is won. Professional production houses maintains a classified directory of talents. Scouting talents is a continuous process and additional names are added to the directory. The producer draws talent taking into account the requirements of the programme on hand. In the case of Drama, the selection is directly related to the characters of the play and the suitability for the particular roles with reference to their voice-age. Completing Contractual Formalities : There may be occasions when the producer has to make use of published material which attracts the copyright law. S/he has to secure the necessary clearances from the copyright holders, as producers do not enjoy any special rights over and above those of ordinary citizens. If the producer proposes to produce a play based on an award winning novel, the media house has to enter into a contract with the author to get the required rights. The organization may have to enter into another contract with the writer who adapts the novel as an audio play. Such clearances may not be required if the copyright law permits it. The producer has to enter into a agreement with everyone who has contributed to the programme; be it a talker, interviewer, interviewee, commentator, participant, writer, drama

artistes, music artiste etc. All these activities become part and parcel of the planning work of the producer.
2.5 PLANNING AN AUDIO DRAMA
A drama producer is always in the lookout for good script covering different themes, including historical and humorous plays. As a drama producer, you will have to persuade well-known writers in your area to write scripts on Production Process specific themes, such as empowerment of women, communal harmony, etc. You will have to look for literary works including works in regional languages which would render themselves well for audio adaptation. You will have to identify writers who can do the adaptation and prepare the script. Planning the cast of artists for participation in the play is equally important. They have to be selected with reference to the roles they have to play keeping in view their voice-age. If the character in a play is of 40 years of age, the artiste selected must have the same voice-age though her/his actual age may be more or less.
2.6 REHEARSALS
The two important steps of production are: rehearsal and recording. Studio time is precious and therefore, before the talker/artists/participants begin recording, they are to be rehearsed. Most of the big media houses have a separate room in the studio complex for rehearsal known as Read Over Room (ROR). This is the first stage of rehearsal without microphone. The second stage of rehearsal is inside the studios with microphones. There would be no need at all or less requirement for post-production, if the producer and the artistes devote adequate time and attention to do proper rehearsals.
2.7 RECORDING / PRODUCTION
After the proper planning and rehearsals the pre-production stage come to an end and now the programme is ready to be recorded which is also known as Production stage. Recording is the responsibility of the producer. It is, therefore, necessary for him/her to check the studio recorder, studio clock and other equipments sufficiently in advance so that there is no hassle at the time of recording. If you have given enough importance to the pre-production part then your production becomes easy. If you have scripted a programme well, checked the content for authenticity, verified its value for the target audience and rehearsed with your artists then the actual production is like a breeze. Studio Recording : Mainly the audio programmes are recorded in a professional recording studio which has got all the technical facilities to record a programme with such a high quality that it is suitable for broadcast or podcast. There are different studios to record different categories of programme like Talk, Music or Drama. The studios are built with such specification that they are most suitable for a particular category of a programme. For example Talk studio will be small and clarity of voice is the main concern, where talks, interviews or discussions are recorded; whereas a music studio will be larger in size, have more reverberation and have scope for more number of microphones. In the same manner the Drama Studio will have its own peculiarities.

2.8 POST PRODUCTION
Post-production, as we discussed earlier, refers to works carried out after the recording process is over. Post-production is essential to remove any imperfections or defects contained in the recording either by oversight of the recordist or by performers / artistes. In spoken word programmes, for example, the speaker may have fumbled at places during his / her speech, Audio Production made some wrong statement and corrected it during the later portion of the speech, or some unwanted sound disturbance may have occurred at some points when the recording session is on. Naturally, you want to remove such unwanted portions in the recording so that the final programme comes out clean and flawless. In a group discussion recording, it may so happen that one of the voices sounds much louder than others, so there is a need to balance the volumes of different speakers at the post-production stage at least, if not done during the production stage itself. Similar pitfalls and disturbances are prone to occur in other kinds of programmes as well - music concerts, audience participation shows, interview programmes etc. We have noted that Audio Editing and Audio Mixing are the two important stages in post- production. Audio Editing consists in removing unwanted portions in the recorded material, altering the sequence of wanted audio clips and reassemble the desperate recorded segments. Mixing denotes to mixing all the audio tracks to make a final master copy of the programme. Once everything has been taken care in terms of direction, production and recording, an overall analysis should be made of the programme. An exhaustive assessment of the entire programme should be made in an objective and detached manner. It is possible that some flaws may have been noticed by the actors/players/participants while recording/production was in process. Certain defects can be edited out from the tape by an ingenious editor and a skilled recordist. A producer must not hesitate to replan/reproduce the entire programme if the assessment reveals that it is not in accordance with the planned objective. 2.9 LET US SUM UP
Audio programs were earlier delivered to people through radio and even today radio is an important mass communication medium. But the advent of the Internet and the increase in its

speed made audio podcasts popular. Be it radio or podcast, both deliver audio programs to listeners. Almost all radio stations also do podcasts. In this unit, you learned that there are four basic components of audio programmes, these are spoken-word, sound effects, music and pause. The importance of these elements was examined. We discussed the attributes of an interesting and informative programme and guidelines for a producer to achieve them. We analysed the pre-requisites in planning an audio programme, and emphasized the importance of the target audience, objectives, content, format, script, and appropriate time slot. The different stages involved in the planning of pre-production and production were analysed.

3.0 INTRODUCTION
Audio podcasts are gradually gaining popularity all over the world. Its listeners are increasing in India too. We have a rich tradition of listening to radio. Hence, there are a large number of fans of audio programmes here. We all enjoy listening to audio programmes but to be able to

write for audio and to produce audio programmes, you must be well versed with the various prevalent audio programming patterns or formats. As you acquire acquaintance with different styles, forms and categories, you will comprehend the fundamentals of audio writing and production as well. This Unit provides brief information about the major formats employed in audio. A conscious attempt has been made to focus more on those formats which are used more in the audio podcasting. However, contemporary trends worldwide have also been included. Attention has also been paid to the emerging changes and evolutions in styles and formats. The unit describes the meaning of the word 'format' in the context of audio programmes.
3.1 LEARNING OUTCOMES
After going through this unit, you will be able to: * discuss the major audio formats; * describe the main characteristics of these formats as well as their sub- formats; and * appreciate the role and importance of these formats in the realm of audio podcasting.
3.2 AUDIO PROGRAMME FORMATS : AN INTRODUCTION
What we essentially mean by the word 'format'? One of the dictionary meanings of this word, when used as a noun, is "the way in which something is arranged or set out and presented". The Cambridge Dictionary defines it as "a pattern, plan or arrangement". Of course, these are traditional meanings. In the digital world, the term 'format' has acquired added and specific connotations. It is derived from the more popularly used word 'form', which denotes a sense of shape, size, structure and configuration. In a creative context, format also encompasses the content being presented in a particular shape or structure, which endows it with a definite narrative style. We can understand this better with the help of some more familiar examples. We say that poetry, short stories, essays and novels are various formats of literature. Similarly, we define classical and light music as two musical formats.
3.2.1 What is Programme Format ?
It is important to realise that the meaning of audio format is the form of a programme employed for various audio platforms. Common people constituting the listeners are concerned with programmes only, which are also the true expression of the best creativity of the audio medium. Creatively speaking the style, structure and pattern of production denotes a particular format. However the first and the foremost factor for a programme to be liked is how good or bad it is essentially as an audio programme.
3.2.2 Basic Audio Formats
You read about the meaning and connotations of the word 'format' by invoking the analogy of the literary formats. If we go on in the same vein, further reflection will make us aware of the fact that all literature can be basically divided into two formats and these are poetry and prose. Poetry can then be further divided into various sub-formats like epic, ballads, blank verse, free verse etc. based on various factors such as length, subject matter, lyricism, style, etc. Similarly,

prose can be divided into novels, short stories, essays, etc. Drama is generally considered a prose format although it might have infusion of poetic elements. Like literature, audio programmes also have two main formats which are Music and Spoken Word. On the basis of importance, extensive public utility and special functionality, some people consider News to be also a separate and distinct format. Audio formats are governed by the fundamental and inherent nature of audio programmes. Audio is a sound medium and it functions within prescribed time-limits. In audio world, the availability or constraints of time can also be a deciding factor in format selection. Although music is a very important area of audio programming, since the main focus of this course is audio podcasts, we'll discuss music-based programs very briefly.
3.3 MUSIC PROGRAMMES ON AUDIO PLATFORMS
Which audio programmes are listened to the most? Ask yourself which programmes are your favourites. The overwhelming possibility is that your answer will be music programmes. Actually a great majority of audio listeners across the world loves listening to music through different audio platforms. Now, each individual is bound to have his or her special likings and these determine as to which music programmes or which genre of music he or she prefers more as a part of his or her listening habits. But it is an undisputed fact that programmes presenting musical selections are globally the most popular audio programmes.
3.3.1 Formats of Music Programmes
We have seen earlier that music constitutes one of the two major and fundamental formats of audio programmes. But music programmes can be further divided or categorised into many sub-formats. Now these sub-formats are not same everywhere. All countries and many societies have their indigenous preferences in terms of which kind or formats of music are more prevalent and popular there. These preferences have a crucial impact on the music programme offerings. As far as our own country India is concerned, the major formats of music programmes here are the following:
1. Classical Music Programmes
2. Light Music Programmes
3. Folk and Tribal Music Programmes
4. Film Music Programmes
5. Western Music Programmes
