1. List any five essential qualities of a good television news anchor.

2. What is voice modulation ?

14.4 ANCHORING FOR DIFFERENT TYPES OF PROGRAMMES
Format and subject of the programme influence anchoring style. In this section, we shall discuss the suitable presentation styles in different types of television news programmes.
14.4.1 Common Formats of News and Role of the Anchor
Some of the common news story formats are as follows: Live : It is when the reporter goes 'live' from the location and a camera is set up to show events as they are unfolding. Usually live news is done for more important stories. The news anchor raises questions about updates which are answered by the reporter. Package : A news package is an audio-visual form of news that has voice overs, bytes, visuals and PTC. The news anchor reads an introduction and then a pre-recorded package is shown. Usually a package is made for the important stories but it can also be used in combination with a 'live' report. Phono : It is usually used for a breaking news or some important update. It is a 'live' report filed in by reporter from scene of the story. Here, the anchor asks questions and reporter replies on phone. Reader : Here, the news anchor reads a story 'on air' with no audio or video elements to support it. Generally, it is used for the less important stories or for 'breaking news' being reported at the last minute. Anchor-Byte : In this format, the anchor reads the news and bytes of the concerned person/s are included. Anchor-Visual : This format contains anchor link and visuals. Anchor reads the news and visuals of that story are played. Generally, this format is used for small stories. You can find this format commonly used in speed/fast news bulletins. Anchor-Graphics : This is similar to Anchor-Visual but here graphics are used in place of video footages. When visuals are not available, this format is used. Here, the anchor reads the news and graphics are shown.
14.4.2 Presentation of Special Bulletins and Shows
Nowadays it is often observed that we have special news bulletins to cater to viewers with specific set of interests. The nature of the programme determines the conduct of its anchor. In the case of special bulletins, an anchor must possess proper knowledge about that specific field. The presentation style varies with the subject of the special bulletin. The list of some categories of special bulletin is as follows: Sports: This category attracts different age groups of viewers. Knowledge, presence of mind and spontaneity are the most important criteria to become a successful sports anchor in India. For example- for a cricket lover, what matters is the way an anchor is able to steer arguments in the show and the input s/he gives to the show.

Crime: You would have come across crime shows or bulletins on television news channels. The show may be totally based on one crime or it may be presented like crime bulletin containing many crime stories. Sometimes crime shows recreate the incident with the help of actors and actresses. This type of show demands a different presentation style other than simple anchoring. Anchors are expected to create suspense and excitement. Business: Some special bulletins or shows focus on news related to stock exchange, industries and other business-related fields. Anchors of these bulletins should have a sound understanding of dynamics of the share market, market economy and other associated areas. Agriculture: This category focuses on the farmers and their major issues like seeds, livestock, pesticides, fertilizers, new agriculture techniques, weather etc. In these shows, anchors should have the capability to connect with farmers and rural folk so that they can communicate the desired messages to them effectively. Fashion and showbiz: More and more people are becoming interested in the lives of film or TV artists, new fashion trends, new make-up related techniques, etc. So, the news channels have also begun to address these fashion and showbiz categories through special shows. Such shows require a different type of anchoring. Here, anchors must act as light hearted and humorous persons. They are also expected to don many fashionable and trendy dresses. Educational and career-based shows: Some news channels have career and education- oriented shows where experts guide the students and job seekers. Religious: A few news channels allocate separate time slots for religious shows especially during festival seasons. While presenting a religious show, the anchors should consciously use appropriate language and dresses. Health: A few special shows or bulletins are based on health related information. They focus on different ailments, their treatments, misconceptions related to different diseases, precautionary measures, fitness issues, etc. At times, you can see the anchor of a Yoga show wearing yoga costumes and even performing yogasanas to attract the viewers' attention. Apart from the above-mentioned categories, you may see some other special shows related to Science and Technology, Automobiles, Film reviews, Travel, etc. Finally, you should understand that the subject of the content decides the presentation style.
14.4.3 Presentation of Talk Shows, Panel Discussions and Debates
Many programmes such as talk shows, panel discussions and news debates require anchors to be fluent, eloquent and spontaneous speakers. For such programmes, while an anchor must have expansive vocabulary, research is also equally important. They must carry out research on the subject of the show beforehand as the anchor is expected to lead the debate or panel discussion. The anchor must have a good command over language. The anchors in talk shows, panel discussions and debates are required to have good observation power and presence of mind to observe and interpret the body language and responses of panellists and experts. Talking to oneself in front of the mirror and describing the points which have to be discussed during the show, can be helpful. Such extempore programmes usually run for a fixed period of time and the anchor who is leading such a show must have a good sense of time as s/he needs to round up the discussion

and draw a sensible conclusion within the stipulated time. The anchor is expected to strictly adhere to the directions given pertaining to the duration that has been set for each segment and commercial breaks. One of the main mistakes evident in the debates and discussions conducted by a novice anchor is the repetition of certain words again and again. Some anchors tend to use interjections at the start of their sentence because they are still thinking about the next sentence they will speak and have not formulated the ideas or questions that they want to ask. Generally, talk shows, discussions and debates are never rehearsed before telecast. During such shows, an anchor has to make use of the good judgment in selection of questions. Before such shows, anchors are expected to sit down with the guest, experts or panellists, to make them comfortable and also ascertain their attitude towards different issues.
14.4.4 Presentation of Interviews
A news anchor should be able to think on his/her feet. While conducting an interview, knowledge and spontaneity play a very important role. Those who are really good at asking questions and interviewing, make it look like they are winging it, but it is the prior preparation that makes it look so smooth and easy. It takes a lot of preparation and persistence to conduct a good interview as an anchor. If you want to conduct a good interview for television news channels, keep the following things in your mind: Make the interviewee comfortable: establishing a rapport /connection with the interviewee will put him/her at ease before the actual interview. Do your homework: while heading towards a discussion with tough questions, a proper research into the issue can be of great help. Listen carefully to the answers as it will help in asking follow up questions. Try to stay away from close ended questions. For Example - if you are interviewing survivor of a natural disaster, you can ask open ended questions along these lines: what were you doing when it happened ? How did you save yourself ? Be persistent: You have to dig for information by rephrasing the same question again and again until you get the answer. Control your emotions: Some interviews may move you to tears or make you angry. But you should learn to hold yourself together and exhibit professionalism. Closing comment: The best way to end an interview is to ask if the interviewee has anything else to add. A new angle may exist that no one else may have thought about.
14.4.5 Presentation of Live and Multi-Anchor Shows
During live shows, an anchor is expected to maintain a link and co-ordination between different participants of the show and the PCR. Live shows and bulletins are more deadline oriented and the anchors must to have a good sense of timing. You may find few shows with more than one anchor. If it is a dual anchor show, then both the anchors are expected to co-ordinate with each other and also with the panellists, experts or participants while receiving instructions from PCR via earpiece. Few channels experiment with more than two anchors also, for example - 'Panchnama' on ABP news. This show is presented by five anchors. Coordination and maintaining the natural flow of the show are main concerns in multi anchor shows.

14.5 WRITING ANCHOR SCRIPT
Once a rundown has been completed or sometimes even before that, the news bulletin producer can start writing anchor scripts of individual news stories. It is also known as anchor link or "The Readers". It is like intro of the report and presented by anchor. You should not squeeze too much information into one or two sentences if it is an anchor link of a news package. If you are writing an anchor link, keep the following things in your mind: You should keep sentences simple and short as it is easier to digest and share idea of the story by using simple and clear information. Difficult words should be written phonetically, and producers should ensure that they point them out in advance. You should be careful with numbers. It is ideal to take big numbers and write them in words to make it easier for anchors to read them in a flow. For example, instead of "the government promises to generate 800000 employment opportunities in next five years," the anchor script should be written, "the government promises to generate 8 lakh employment opportunities in next five years." You should avoid passive voice sentences and use conversational tone. Anchor script should be written in active voice and should appear as if the anchor is speaking to the viewers. Using conversational tone is very important to establish connect with the viewers. It should not appear as if the anchor is just reading from the teleprompter. You should try to use compelling words in anchor links. The viewers should be hooked to watch the whole report or segment after hearing the anchor link. Share main idea of the news report. Try to identify specific W questions that you should provide answers to in the readers/anchor links. Try to introduce the name of the reporter while writing anchor link of a news report. If s/he is reporting live in an area, recognize that so and so is reporting live and specify name in the script as well if it is an exclusive report as the reporter deserves the credit. Television news anchoring demands a lot of hard work, sincerity, perseverance and knowledge. Knowledge about different fields and current affairs, command over language, ability of multitasking, knowledge of journalistic ethics and laws, voice modulation and skill to handle teleprompter are a few essential qualities required for a good television news presenter. The format and content of the programme influence the style of anchoring. In this Unit, we also discussed the anchoring styles for different programme formats as well as for the special bulletins based on different subjects like sports, business, crime, etc. Writing for anchor scripts has also been discussed. A good anchor script helps in better anchoring.

5.0 INTRODUCTION
Today, communication via social media is not just about sharing information, it also involves influencing opinions and building relationships. Social media users are connected with thousands of people over the internet. Now, businesses and other service providers can reach their consumers in a faster, more segmented and more predictable way. This new online ecosystem has opened unlimited possibilities for business development and product advocacy. Online advocacy and outreach programmes are two powerful tools for businesses or organisations to create awareness among customers, and strengthen their digital presence using different online platforms. In this unit, we will explore how this new media is helping advertisers to engage with the target audience to advocate for their brands.
5.1 LEARNING OUTCOMES
Through this Unit, you are expected to learn about: * Dimensions of online advocacy; * Various aspects of media outreach; and * Need for online advocacy in today's time.
5.2 ONLINE ADVOCACY

In general, advocacy is anything that supports the betterment of the community and society. Media advocacy is defined as using mass media strategically to advance public policy initiatives. Media advocacy is rooted in community advocacy. Big companies use it to promote their brands through strategic planning for concerning areas or within their competence.
5.2.1 DEFINITION AND TYPES
The use of social media helps companies in marketing to support a particular message or cause in a more specific way. Contrary to commercial advertising, advocacy advertising is considered to be in the interest of a group or the public, and is generally not profitable. Online advertising is the strategic planning of advertisements to advocate any policy or awareness among the target consumer through online campaigns. The company can introduce the website, emails, and social media platforms such as Facebook, Instagram, YouTube, to source new advocates from the on-line community or the target digital consumers. It creates virtual content material to explain the campaign, its goals, and why it matters. Online users who engage with the content or provide their information for detailed study may become sturdy advocates of the company's or organisation's motives. This is what is called Digital Advocacy. Every person's needs and wants are specific. Their desire for helping may vary in nature and degree, and can change in the course of their lives. These different needs and progressions have led to the evolution of different variations of advocacy. These are as follows:
Source: Twitter
* Case advocacy: Any business may represent any person, group, or organisation in a 'case advocacy' situation. For instance, the coconut oil manufacturer Shalimar has supported commercials in honour of female cancer survivors who lost their hair after treatment. It was really interesting that a renowned business, known for its hair oil, featured a bald woman getting ready to go to work and continue her duties. * Paid independent advocacy: This is a two-step or multi-step communication. Nowadays on Instagram, YouTube and on other social media platforms, social media influencers are giving reviews of different kinds of products, hacks etc. These social influencers are asked to review products like apps, beauty products, electronic gadgets, and the like. These influencers do advocacy in favour of certain companies. * Self-advocacy: Sometimes, we have witnessed that any individual is giving the review of any hotel or restaurant on their social media profile and tagging the organisation or service providers. It is one kind of self-advocacy in which social media influencers play a great role.

* Peer advocacy: Peer advocacy means to give response from the same state of condition or mind. If you are making friends and facing the same issue or problem, you may share your experience with them. For example, in a travel group on Facebook, you ask about a good hotel, which is also budget friendly. Many people, or peers, will reply to your queries, advocating for the hotel. * Citizen advocacy: This typically means that when a trained volunteer reaches out to, or advocates for, other members of a community, or the community itself. Citizen advocates speak out on behalf of people who may face challenges in speaking up for themselves. A good example of this is the website Change.org, which allows users to craft, sign and share petitions on urgent social issues to highlight them. * Statutory advocacy: It means when a person or an organisation is statutorily responsible to advocate on any issue or on any incident. For example, different banks or police departments promote campaigns for cybersecurity.
5.2.2 NEED OF ONLINE ADVOCACY
For non-profits of all sizes, online advocacy is turning into an increasingly effective choice. Online advocacy campaigns, anchored around raising awareness or mobilising political and social help, provide immense benefits to the non-profit sector nowadays. The reasons for its increasing use are: * It introduces a brand's importance (and necessity) for online engagement of non-profits. * Surging public interest and recognition around missions associated with social, financial, public health, and other issues. * It ensures improved digital engagement across the board, reaching the urban as well as remote corners of the country. Online advocacy will frequently focus on connected topics including politics, economic issues, and social issues. For example, a company that wants to introduce a drug treatment programme for a community may also launch a marketing campaign to attract investors and funding agencies for their capacity-building and increasing production capacity. If a local politician has expressed worries about the programme and the medication, and decides to support an opponent, the campaign may turn into political debate and discussion rather than being an advocacy for action.
5.2.3 PLANNING OF ONLINE ADVOCACY
Decentralised and people-centric methods that empower supporters to act on their own are exceptionally effective in these days' virtual panorama. On your advocacy marketing campaign, your advocates will assist in promoting your marketing campaign, raise consciousness online, and facilitate discussions between supporters. Let us now try and understand the process of recruiting and empowering advocates. * Look first at your existing support system: Firstly, enlist advocates who can assist from the outset before commencing the advocacy effort. Determine who is most likely to be most enthusiastic about customer relationship management (CRM) and volunteer management systems, and then reach out to them. Reliable volunteers could be on the lookout for fresh ways to engage with the concerned project in a meaningful way, and their enthusiasm and vigour could help fuel your campaign. * Create a lead marketing campaign to recruit new advocates: Use the company's website, web portals, emails, blog, vlogs and social media posts to search for new advocates from your online community. Create virtual content explaining your advocacy campaign and its objective. Online customers who interact with your content material or offer their inputs will be encouraged to become strong advocates of your purpose. * Empower the advocates with the right resources: When a company recruits advocates and launches its campaign, they want to achieve success. Presenting a directory of appropriate sources

on the website or on social media is a good idea, as is web-hosting one or more virtual training programmes to speak about the marketing campaign's goals in a better manner. Non-official letter templates and sample social media posts might be useful for your advocates as well. * Look for different guidance resources your advocates might leverage: For instance, corporate partners, irrespective of size, can assist the advocacy marketing campaign by amplifying the message, sponsoring a virtual outreach event, making donations, or by providing monetary contributions to items made by personnel. * Customise the content whenever accumulating information: For online advocacy campaigns to yield lengthy-term advantages for the company, they should have the appropriate resource material such as statistics, data, sources, and the like. * Set relevant key performance indicators (KPIs): One challenge in advocacy is that it could be difficult to demarcate degrees of progress to achieve your goal of effecting change (as opposed to achieving concrete fundraising targets in a regular campaign). With the aid of setting applicable key performance signs early within the planning process, you may overcome this issue. Indicators such as total number of signatures, new supporter acquisition, and online engagement metrics are all beneficial KPIs for advocacy, but you must set yours based on the specifics of your campaign. * Spend enough time in planning: It can be tempting to simply recruit advocates, launch your marketing campaign, and let the campaign run on its own. However, the right thing to do would be to adopt a hands-on approach; be proactive and plan everything in a detailed manner. Give thorough thought to how you will attain new audiences, what you will ask your supporters to do, what you will do when you have accomplished your goal, and how you will improve your potential of making a tangible change. Here is a visual representation of the steps mentioned above.
5.2.4 EFFECTIVENESS OF ON-LINE ADVOCACY
Rohit Bhargava, prolific author, former adman and brand strategist, and founder of Non-Obvious, provides us with a host of reasons why advocacy may be more powerful than advertising per se. Advocacy, he writes, * Overcomes barriers of distance and national borders. * Makes it less difficult for "observers" to take part. * Gives you a vacation spot to area all supporting content and messages to alternate minds.

* Reduces the need for celebrities, politicians and governments to raise problem profiles. * Provides more engaging ways to communicate with the target audience.. * Encourages word of mouth communication and affords more venues for messages to travel virally. * Allows people to show support for complex social or political issues anonymously. * Encourages "impulse" donations and makes it easier for groups to control donations. Let us explain this using an example: * In December 2017, Zomato's outdoor ad campaign took the social media by storm for its use of puns and witty references. The food delivery app came up with billboards with slogans with pop culture references like, "Oonchi hai building? Left teri band hai", "Mera pizza ghar aaya o Ram ji" and so on. The campaign became a hit with the public, and numerous social media users posted images of billboards in their cities. However, one of the billboards used abbreviations that are widely seen as expletive words. This drew a huge public backlash, with several people condemning the app for its usage of swear words. Zomato hastily took down these explicitly-worded billboards, and apologised to the public. But, it capitalised on this fiasco with another brilliant strategy. This time, they offered something called the "Outrage Discount Code," a playful compensation for causing offence to the public, by declaring a "10% cashback on your next order, use promo code OUTRAGE when you pay online." The brand was lauded for its handling of a disastrous situation with grace and a sense of fairness. Additionally, it lent the brand's image a certain degree of humility and authenticity, by accepting the public's sentiments. Check Your Progress: 1 Note: 1) Use the space below for your answers.

5.3 ONLINE OUTREACH
Outreach in marketing means to influence a certain category of influential people of the society who can motivate other people to act in a certain manner. Today, social media users produce blogs, vlogs and posts on Instagram and other platforms to reach out their target audience. Similarly, big companies are using the strategy of online outreach to communicate with their target consumer directly with the intention of a more focussed marketing.
5.3.1 DEFINITION

There are various kinds of definitions of outreach marketing. In this chapter, we are discussing digital or online outreach programmes, which is why an explanation of it by the UK-based company Extradigital is very interesting. According to Extradigital, online outreach is the process of reaching out to the right people at the right place and at the right time through the Internet for the brand awareness of the company. Digital outreach strategy helps a company to connect with the people and make them feel that they, too, are an important part of the brand.
5.3.2 NEED OF OUTREACH PROGRAMME
Developing a business is not an easy task; the younger the business, the greater the need to reach out widely to clients and customers. Although initially one may see little to no growth, a push in the right direction can make a world of difference, and soon. Outreach marketing is one of the simplest advertising and marketing techniques to achieve that, allowing visibility and a building of trust. In order to build concrete relationships with people and communities, online outreach helps in ways such as these: * Sustainable relation-making: Media presence is important for any brand marketing. How to reach the target and how to attract them is important for any brand. Smartphones are an indispensable part of modern life. Especially during COVID pandemic, dependency on smartphones and social media increased a hundredfold. So, if a brand can communicate with its audience digitally, it can make a strong relationship with its consumers. * Personalised communication through different platforms: The digital habits of accessing programmes or content is very easy to understand now. There are several parameters which can measure the user's preference in content searching. A company can reach the target group easily and can customise the message according to the user's interests. * Empowerment: Many new start-ups use social media platforms like Facebook and Instagram to create new customers. Facebook owner Mark Zuckerberg introduced Facebook 'Meta' as the new horizon of digital marketing. There are many groups which have empowered the users to create a new community of buyers and sellers as well. * Market visibility: The key benefit of online outreach is that a company or an organisation does not need to bring their customer out of their comfort zone. Users can access all kinds of information from the web, or book any product or service on their personal devices. So, a brand can be present and reinforced digitally, reminding the users of its product throughout the day. * Authenticity: In many cases, on e-commerce platforms, reviews of a product of any brand can be seen easily. These reviews are given by the users of that product. They impact the perception of the probable buyers and are highly sought and followed. This kind of interactivity helps to build an authentic image among the users. * Right customers with right information: SEO (Search Engine Optimiser) is the new magic tool for any brand. If a user is searching any kind of product or service on different search-engines, SEO helps to attract the attention of your target consumer towards your brand. So, the company can reach the right customer at the right time with the right information. See the new clipping below for an example of organisational outreach:

5.3.3 OUTREACH PROGRAMME FOR CUSTOMERS
This business strategy is used by a company or organisation to create a good relationship with individual customers. Before taking a product or service to a customer through an outreach programme, a company or an organisation needs to create a potential customer profile. This is done by understanding the customer's previous purchase patterns, social media activity, and other such details. Then, what one needs is to select the proper channel to reach them, using strategies designed by the company's outreach marketing team.
5.3.4 OUTREACH PROGRAMME FOR THE COMMUNITY
Many companies undertake outreach programmes aimed at different sections of the society. Such initiatives are not about buying or selling products; rather it is about building a good image in the community. It helps in promoting brands in indirect ways. For example, Tata has outreach programmes focussing on education, environment, health, and so on. Further, corporate social responsibility (CSR) is an important form of outreach programmes, initiated by corporate companies to connect with the public by tending to the community's needs. A good example of this is Hindustan Unilever Limited's "Project Shakti," which focuses on women empowerment by providing livelihood to women in rural India.
5.3.5 HOW TO PLAN AN OUTREACH PROGRAMME
In order to successful execute an outreach programme, there are a few steps one must follow:
1. Figuring out the company's own plan:
Every company has its own target consumer and own brand management strategy. A company that is interested in G.T. (General Trade) marketing will be much more interested in traditional outreach programmes. But companies that are interested in M.T. (Modern Trade) marketing, or in e-commerce, may give their primary focus to online outreach programmes. For a successful online outreach programme, among the most important prerequisites are: * Know the audience: Companies can choose influencers or make web content based on the tastes of their audience. * Know the aim: The aim may be to improve the brand's image or to improve sales or to grab a larger market. So before going online, the aim should be clear to the marketing team. * Activity: Your ideal influencer wishes to be lively on social media. In the event they haven't published, blogged, or tweeted in a long time, chances are that they don't have a fresh target market. Even if they're on board with promoting your content, they're already at a deficit and may not possibly gain your enterprise a lot of traffic. * Relevance: This really means that the influencer you pick must be related to your business in a few ways. As an example, in case you promote content material on a software or an app, your best influencer has to be connected to online organisations and audiences in a key issues.

* Recognition: Contrary to what you may think, your influencer need not to be very famous. When you have interaction in outreach marketing, consider it as a two-way avenue. Your influencer could be much more likely to accompany you if they feel you'll be capable of helping them. With this in mind, pick an influencer with a good following, but more importantly, someone who has the room to grow. * Engagement: Look at the target markets your influential associates have. Do their posts have likes, retweets, and feedback? Does the influencer reply to remarks and create a conversation with their fans? Follower counts are vital if you want to understand if the influencer is as engaged with their fans as their fans are with them. * Dating constructing: After you've identified an influencer, reach out to them via e-mail or on their most lively social media platform. You can pitch your concept for a partnership with them. When crafting your pitch, make sure to be clear, concise, and to highlight the benefits your influencer stands to achieve from partnering with you.
2. Attract the target audience:
* Improve SEO: One of the most important advantages of online outreach is that a company or any organisation can improve their SEO (Search Engine Optimizer) through SERPs (Search Engine Results Pages) by paying a certain amount of money to search engine companies, such as Google, Yahoo, etc. Here, we need to remember that money is not only the factor for the improvement of the SEOs. The content of the linking website or web pages are the second most important factors for SEO. (https://directiveconsulting.com/case-studies/) * Promote the content: Other than assisting you with expanding your hunt traffic (digital marketing efforts to to attract website visitors), outreach advertising can assist you with advancing your substance. Most website proprietors are battling to advance their content. More often than not, content intensification for them is just a question of distributing another blog entry and sharing it via virtual entertainment.
3. Expand your Network and engage the audience
A key aspect of marketing is the "Positioning" of the product or the message. In online brand marketing, positioning the content of your brand is a life tool. For this, you need to choose the proper communication online platform. The headline of the content should be a catchy one. The company may send newsletters or emails to the target consumers. The company may ask for a referral like Swiggy or Goibibo or even G-pay. Nowadays, very often we find few online surveys when we scroll through Facebook or YouTube. This is one of the effective ways to engage the consumers.
4. Maintain the communication
After the introduction of a proper outreach plan, it is necessary to follow-up the programme. In most cases, users log in with their email ids or mobile numbers or with both on search-engines, or on any digital platforms. With this, users generally click the option which enables the company or organisation to send notifications. These notifications are the most helpful tool to reach the customers, while in many cases, companies email newsletters. Not only do they introduce the brand, they also send updates to their target customer or consumers.
5. Galvanise
Through such outreach programmes, a company convinces the consumers and creates a good image among them. Here is a visual representation of the steps mentioned above

5.4 ADVOCACY VERSUS OUTREACH PROGRAMME
There is no such conflict between advocacy and the outreach programmes undertaken by different companies or organisations. The main aim of advocacy is to get support of the consumers for a sustainable cause. By using digital platforms, companies are trying to get more support for their brands. The outreach programme also helps in promoting brands but in a different way. It reaches the consumer with the aim of public good. 5.0 INTRODUCTION
Audio-visual programs are very popular among people all over the world. This medium (audio- visual) takes precedence over other media as it stimulates multiple sensory organs of the audiences. Unlike print or radio, television and film production combine to employ visual, audio as well as graphical tools to disseminate information. The never-ending soap operas and cookery shows keep the audiences hooked to their screens; comedy and sports entertain the male audiences and animation and children's programmes attract the attention of the younger audience. While television programmes create a fictional world that provide the audiences an escape mode from their immediate realities, they also bring real life incidences through news and reality TV. In the last few years, reality TV formats, in particular, have been very successful for audiences as well as producers. Through game shows, talent hunt and docusoaps, Reality TV has established itself as a strong opponent of the popular soap opera format. Talent hunt shows, in particular, have aided in giving a platform to young talents and honing their skills. While some formats cater to a specific segment of audiences, others are universally enjoyed by a diverse set of audience. In this unit, we'll discuss various popular programme formats used in audio- visual media.

5.1 LEARNING OUTCOMES
After reading this unit, you will be able to: * understand the audio-visual programme formats; * differentiate between various fiction and non-fiction audio-visual programme formats; and * describe the key characteristics of each programme format.
5.2 UNDERSTANDING PROGRAMME FORMATS
A programme format is a complex structure that offers both sameness and variety. In simple words, a format is the organizational framework that facilitates the making of a programme. Imagine yourself preparing your favourite recipe in the kitchen. You will first assemble all the necessary ingredients required for the recipe and then follow a cooking method. The cooking method will describe the proportion of ingredients to be used, which ingredients to be used first and which ones to be used later and the time taken to prepare the recipe. If you miss out on any step, your recipe may taste different. Similarly, programme formats are like recipes. They provide the guidelines that help in making one programme different from the other and if not followed properly may confuse the audiences and not fulfill their expectations. Albert Moran in his study of television formats states that a TV format is "that set of invariable elements in a programme out of which the variable elements of an individual episode are produced" (2006: 20). It is the "crust of the pie" that remains the same throughout but offers "new fillings" every week (Moran, 1998:13). In simpler terms, a programme format is like a rule-book that offers the producers a list of do's and dont's. These programme formats are often adapted in different languages by producers across the globe. The TV format adaptations fall into two broad categories - fiction and non-fiction. While TV programmes like Who Wants to Be a Millionaire, Big Brother, Fear Factor, The Voice, Masterchef etc. would fall into the category of non-fiction formats; programmes like 24, Jassi Jaisi Koi Nahi etc. are fiction-formats. In fiction formats, the producers can exercise some amount of flexibility but in non-fiction programme formats, the producers may have to follow the rulebook as it is. In industry language, a format refers to a structural layout that allows both the rigidity of following certain rules and the flexibility of adaptation in different languages.

Before we discuss the different kinds of programming formats, there is another term that needs some attention - 'genre'. While both the terms 'format' and 'genre' are closely related and often misunderstood to be the same, it is important for us to understand the difference between the two.
5.3 PROGRAMME FORMATS: DIFFERENT TYPES
Audio-visual programme formats can be classified into the following two categories:
5.3.1 Fiction Formats
Most of entertainment TV is dominated by fiction formats. The word 'fiction' is borrowed from literature and refers to any kind of literature that has been created through imagination. It consists of stories about people, places and events that are imaginary. At times, fiction may also take inspiration form real life incidents that are adapted into imaginary settings. In television, fiction formats refer to all kinds of enetrtainment forms that are not real and take inspiration from the imagination of the creators of the programme. We can further sub-divided fiction formats into drama, comedy, soap operas, crime shows, children's programmes to name a few. The audiences prefer watching fiction because it provides them an escape from their immediate realities and offers them an experience of an imaginary world that they often aspire to be a part of. Let us now look at some fiction formats that are popular on television and try to analyze some key characteristics of each format.
1. SITCOM : Situation Comedy (sitcom) is a classic fiction format on television whose roots
belong to radio. A situation comedy plot usually has a stable set of characters (with one or two guest appearances at times) who face a new crisis or situation that they deal with in every episode. In other words, there is no conitnuing plot unlike sopa operas and audiences can catch up from any episode and still be familiar with the characters and plot. The sitcom format uses a studio that has one or two sets build where the entire show takes place. For example, the popular American sitcom F.R.I.E.N.D.S. follows the life of six friends who live in a New York apartment. Most parts of the sitcom are shot in the apartment and the neary cafe Central Perk where the friends socialize. As John Hartley describes sitcoms combine "comic talent with dramatic chracter and action" (2015: 97). They either put funny actors into a dramatic situation or put an ensemble cast to bring out humour. Sitcoms are either shot in front of a live studio audience or use canned laughter /recorded laughter that is insterted in between the episodes and provides a cue to the audiences.

Family sitcoms are a popular format on Indian television. Some very popular family sitcoms on TV include Khichdi, Sarabhai Vs. Sarabhai, Tarak Metha Ka Ulta Chashma and Bhabhi Ji Ghar Par Hain. While Khichdi narrates the story of a joint family with funny characters, Sarabhai Vs. Sarabhai showcases the everyday banter between the mother-in-law and the daughter-in-law. Tarak Mehta and Bhabhi ji mainly deal with neighbourhood chracaters who take a dig at each other. Indian audiences have appreciated these shows and hence a demand for the format has always dominated the market. Use of catchphrases is a commonplace in sitcoms where certain characters use some phrases over and over again so that when the charcater appears on-screen the audiences start to recognise it. While they provide the audiences some relief through humour, they also impart moral lessons. Sometimes few sitcoms use sexual innuendos and cheap humour that makes them unworthy of watching with family. In a sitcom, even the most serious problem is dealt with in a humorous manner and does not sustain for a long time unlike in soap opera narratives. Similarly, workplace sitcoms have also emerged as a popluar genre. In these sitcoms the workplace takes the place of the family and office colleagues replace family members. Programmes like Office Office, F.I.R. etc are an example of the workplace sitcoms. While the former has a set up of a government office, the latter takes place in a police station. They often take digs at the government, system and society at large.
2. SOAP OPERA : For decades soap operas have remained the mainstay of television.
Generally considered as a women's fiction-form, soap operas have never-ending narratives and multiple plotlines. Like sitcoms, soap operas have also originated from radio. The word 'soap' refers to the commercial sponsorships that detergent companies gave to American radio stations during 1930s. Since these radio soaps were broadacst during daytime when most of the audiences would include women, they came to be known as a women's genre. All soap operas rely on the serial form that allows the possibility of extending a fictional narrative over many years without providing any closure. American and British soaps like Dynasty and Days of Our Lives have been on air for decades. Indian soap operas like Kyunki Saas bhi Kabhi Bahu Thi were also aired for many years. Soap opera narratives generally deal with stories of families and focus on interpersonal relationships where characters discuss marital, romantic and family problems. When one issue is resolved, another emerges providing non-closure of the narrative. They trigger our emotional quotient and are melodramatic in form.

Since the soap operas have female audiences, female progtanists centralize the narrative while male characters play supporting roles. The moral universe of a sopa opera showcases a struggle between good and evil where good emerges victorious. This good and evil is often portrayed by the heroine vs. vamp dyad. In Indian soap operas, this is portrayed through the daughter-in- law vs. mother-in-law dyad more commonly referred to as saas vs. bahu. Indian sopa oeras are alternatively also known as saas-bahu dramas. Since the invasion of satellite TV channels, Indian sopa operas have also captured the prime- time slots and have gained immense success. They are the primary revenue generators for any TV channel. Prime-time soap oeras are different from daytime soap operas in that they also take consideration of male audiences and do have important roles played by male characters but women still dominate the scene. Television producer Ekta Kapoor is considered to have revolutionized Indian TV with saas-bahu dramas also known as K-serials like Kyunki Saas Bhi Kabhi Bahu Thi, Kahaani Ghar Ghar Ki and Kitne Achche Lagte Hain to name a few. These soap operas shifted focus from middle-class families to rich families leading glamorous lives. While these soaps were appreciated by the audiences for sometime, the audiences were soon bored with them and a new genre of soaps with social messages emerged. Balika Vadhu a soap that demonstrated the evil customs of child marriage and Na Aana Is Des Lado about female infanticide soon left the K-serials behind. Even today soap opears dominate Indian TV screens and are popular amongst audiences.
3. Children's Programmes : Children's TV programmes are an important category as they
are not defined by the media text but by the audiences who watch these programmes. Children's TV can range from animation to educational programmes and aim at entertaining and educating the children. While they address children as their primary audience, adult audiences also seem to enjoy some programmes. These programmes are usually slotted either on Sunday mornings or early evenings on weekdays when children return from school. Speaking of Indian television, both public service broadcaster Doordarshan and private satellite channels have fostered the growth of children's TV. In the early 1990s, Doordrashan telecast children's programmes in collaboration with NCERT and CIET. One of the programmes telecast by them was Tarang that was combination of entertainment and education. Doordrashan also telecast many entertainment shows like Shaktiman, Gali Gali Sim Sim, Malgudi Days and Potli Baba Ki amongst others. Amongst these Shaktiman emerged as the first Indian superhero for Indian kids who only knew Superman and Spiderman until the late

1990s. Dordarshan also imported a series Meena from Bangladesgh developed with the help of UNICEF that touched upon issues of social equality and gender through a caricature of the character Meena. With the coming of satellite TV, Children's TV expanded furthermore in India. There were more number of programmes that catered to children like a fantasy fiction Sonpari, animated series Chhota Bheem, Derek O' Brien's Bournvita Quiz Contest to name a few. Soon, there emerged a number of imported children's programmes dubbed in Hindi language like Small Wonder, I Dream of Genie and Different Strokes to name a few. Currently, there are dedicated channels for children like Nickelodeon, POGO and Cartoon Network. Children's TV formats are a great source of revenue for broadcasters as they create a market for merchandize like toys, t-shirts, books etc. Perhaps, this is why children's TV is often criticized for exploiting the young consumers and their parents. Reality Shows that feature children like Saregamapa Lil Champs, Indian Idol Junior, Masterchef Junior and Kya Aap Paanchvi Paas se Tez Hain can also be considered as part of Children's TV as they feature children as contestants. But they are also enjoyed equally by adult audiences. Children's TV is a lucrative genre and is enjoyed equally by kids as well as the adults in the family.
4. Web Series : With the popularity of over-the-top (OTT) platforms like ZEE5, Netflix,
Amazon Prime etc. a new format that has become popular amongst the audiences is that of the web series. Depending upon the plotline, they may fall into several categories like romance, crime, drama, comedy etc. The narrative of a web series lasts for several seasons (generally three to five) with each season having a finite number of episodes. This characteristic of narrative closure with finite episodes makes the audiences indulge in a phenomenon commonly referred to as binge-watching wherein the audiences tend to watch back-to-back episodes and finish the series at one go. Web series have also introduced a wave of fresh content for the audiences who were bored of watching regular saas-bahu dramas on television. Many shows have been critically acclaimed by the audiences. Known for their edgy content, exceptional production quality, good casting and unconventional storylines, the web series have given a new lease of life to entertainment. The audiences of these web series are often the young male and female audiences who consume content on their smartphones or tablets. Since these programmes are typically streamed on online platforms, they often include bold content which may not be suitable for family

audiences or children. Taking advantage of no censorship rules on online platforms, some producers have also crossed the line and offered obscene content to the audiences. But barring a few, most of the web series content has been a welcome change and has raised the bar of television entertainment. 5.3.2 Non-Fiction Formats
Non-fiction or Reality TV has been both a boon and a bane for TV entertainment. The rise of satellite TV in the early 1990s gave a push to Reality TV formats with music-based shows like Meri Awaz Suno and Antakshari and game shows like Tol Mol Ke Bol winning hearts of the audiences. At the turn of the century, with Kaun Banega Crorepati, Reality TV made a grand entry on Indian TV screens and since then there has been no looking back. Today, every entertainment channel's weekend slots are full of Reality TV content most of which are adapted versions of their foreign counterparts. Reality TV hit chords with Indian middle-class audiences who thought it was their one-way ticket to fame, success and money. It provided opportunity to common people who had some kind of talent to look glamorous and appear on national TV. Many celebrities have built their careers from reality TV whether it is in the field of singing, cooking or dancing. One of the criticisms of Reality TV is that it is not always real. Scenes are often scripted and constructed to enhance the entertainment value which puts the 'real' at stake. It therefore undervalues the intelligence quotient of audiences by offering them 'constructed reality' or

'mediated reality' in the name of reality. The presence of the camera itself is questioned as it is belived that people don't behave their trueselves in front of the camera. More of these issues will be discussed as we move on to discuss the different programme formats in Reality TV. Non-fiction or reality TV is a broad category that covers different kind of formats under its umbrella like news, game/quiz shows, talent hunt, docusoaps and talk shows to name a few. Let us now look at some popular formats to understand Reality TV in greater detail.
1. News : Television news is a non-fiction format that may not be considered as a form of
entertainment or Reality TV. It is considered as a "window on the world" that gives us updated information about the world we live in. While news follows ethical standards, it is often understood as mediated reality rather than being completely real. It is presented in various formats like a bulletin, an analysis, an interview or a group discussion. Most news formats are of half -an-hour duration. A news bulletin is usually presented by one or two anchors who present the headlines follwed by a detailed information about each of the news items. These news items are often reported by journalists or reporters who are present on-ground. While political news is the mainstay of a news bulletin, it also covers international news, business news, human-interest stories, sports, entertainment and weather updates. An analysis usually covers an in-depth enquiry on any one topic which is usually related to current-affairs. One or two anchors in the studio unfold the entire news item through the use of graphics, ground reports, intreviews etc. to give the audiences a comprehensive understanding about the issue. For example an analysis on "Annual Budget" will first unfold details about the budget, how it is going to be advantageous for certain sectors and disadvantageous for other. It will also include interviews of Finance Minister, opposition leaders, economy experts etc. and vox-pops of common public regrading their views on the budget. An analysis aims at providing all pros and cons related to an issue. An interview is usually a one-on-one discussion between an interviewer/anchor and an interviewee/subject expert. The interviewer poses certain questions to the inetrviewee about the related topic and interviewee responds accordingly. The interviewer must ensure that he/she gives enough opportunity to the expert to express his views and remains neutral throughout the course of the inetrview. A group discussion is similar to an interview, the only exception being that the number of discussants increase. Unlike an interview, a group discussion involves people from different perspectives to come on a common platform and discuss the pros and cons of an issue. The discussion is moderated by an anchor who poses questions to each

participant. This format is often considered very noisy and sometimes disliked by audiences since speakers often overlap each other. Until the 1990s the public broadcaster Doordrashan was the only news broadcaster that broadcast news bulletins at specific times in a day. With the coming of satellite TV and increasing competition, twenty-four hour news channels became popular. Private satellite channels like Aaj Tak, NDTV, Zee News, India TV and many others now compete in the same space. Even Doordrashan has a dediacted twenty-four hour news channel, DD News. With more advanced technologies, LIVE broadcasting has become commonplace amongst news channels. Increasing competition, while on the one hand, provides a diversity of news, on the other, has also led to the trend of Breaking News that has severely compromised with ethical journalistic standrads.
2. Documentaries : Documentaries present reality through real characters, real documents and
real visuals. It is a very popular non-fiction audio-visual format used for TV and OTT platforms. Documentaries can be produced on a wide range of issues, from wildlife to politics.
3. Game / Quiz Shows : You must have seen Bollywood superstar Amitabh Bachchan asking
questions to contestants seated on a hot seat in the popular TV show Kaun Banega Crorepati (KBC, hereafter). On every correct answer, the contestant wins some amount of money and on a wrong answer s/he gets eliminated. This is the basic format that any quiz show follows. A quiz master asking questions and participants responding in shortest time possible. Bournvita Quiz Contest hosted by Derek O' Brien is considerd to be one of the first in this format. In BQC, school students were paired in teams of two and competed against each other. The team that answered maximum correct answers was declared the winner. Following the succes of KBC, there were many other shows like Kya Aap Paanchvi Paas se Tez Hain, Kamzor Kadi Kaun etc. that tested the knowledge of the contestanst in lieu of some prize money. Most of these, however, were adapatations of Western game formats. These shows generally test the intelligence quotient of the contestant without getting into more personal details. For the audiences, quiz shows are highly interactive as they allow the possibility of play-along where the audiences also test their own intelligence. In fact, contemporary shows like KBC have increased audience interactivity through SMS by involving the audiences to play along and win prizes. Quiz formats are knowledge-based formats that assure the audiences that they can make it big solely on the basis of their knowledge.

Game shows, like quiz shows, focus on competition and monetary gain. However, they may not test the text-book knowledge of contestants in doing so. Game shows are more entertaining in nature and involve contestants in fun activities like guessing the price of a commodity, solving a jig-saw puzzle, aiming an arrow on a shooting board etc. Tol Mol Ke Bol inspired by the American version The Price is Right was one of the earliest game show formats. Another one that became popular in Early 2000s was Khul Ja Sim Sim that demanded the audiences to guess the correct price of a commodity to take it home. There are also some other shows like Dus Ka Dum, Sab Khelo Sab Jeeto and Minute to Win it that fall under the same category.
4. Talent Hunt : Talent Hunt shows are a popular format on weekend television. The unique
selling proposition of a talent hunt format is the talent that the contestants bring on the platform
- singing, dancing, cooking or acting. They are competition-based formats that showcase the
talent of the competitors and ensure that the best talent wins. As mentioned earlier Meri Awaz Suno a singing-talent show on Doordarshan was the first of its kind that nurtutred singing talent. In contemporary television, there are a plethora of talent shows each showcasing a particular talent. While there are singing talent shows like Indian Idol, The Voice, Saregamapa , there are also dance talent shows like Dance India Dance, Superdancer etc. A cooking talent show Masterchef India became very popular amongst audiences as for the first time they witnessed a cooking face-off on television. Shows like India's Got Talent give platform to multiple kinds of talents including singing, acting, dancing etc. Many of these shows were so popular that they have had multiple seasons on air. The format of a talent show is based on tough competition and a weekly elimination of the weakest contestant resulting in a winner at the end of the show. The contestants participate not only to showcase their talent but also to attain celebrity status, fame and money. The narrative of the show follows the journey of a participant from being a nobody to somebody. Audiences are hooked to the participants' journey and start connecting emotionally with them. The back- stage reportage of the contestants' rehearsals, their nervousness before a performance, dressing-up in the green-room and their interactions with other contestants and mentors is also an important aspect of talent hunt shows. The show is judged by a panel of judges who are veterans in their respective fields. These judges are often film celebrities who add a glamour quotient to the show. Many film stars like Madhuri Dixit, Shilpa Shetty, Salman Khan and Akshay Kumar have taken the role of a judge in Talnet hunt shows. Oftentimes, the audience voting is also combined with judges' decision

in eliminating contestants. Along with superlative talent, chemistry between the judges, contestants and the host is what makes a show entertaining.
5. Docusoaps : As the name suggests docusoaps are a TV format that take inspiration from
documentaries and soap operas. However, unlike documentary films, docusoaps focus not so much on information and education but more on drama, conflict and entertainment. This format uses documentary techniques like 'fly on the wall' approach, hand-held camera movements and soap opera techniques like fast-paced editing and alternating between narratives. Under this format, audiences get a sneak-peek into the private lives of individuals/families/celebrities. Docusoaps primarily use the method of surveillance to observe indiviudals, thus providing voyueristic pleasures to audiences. At times, the format also uses hidden cameras for more unobtrusive behaviour from the participants.
6. Talk Shows : Talk shows are an important feature of entertainment television and
television's own way of creating a 'public sphere'. They range form being social, cultural as well as political in nature. While most political shows can be considered under the news format, social and cultural may fall under this category. The format centralizes the individual/guest who has achieved something extraordinary or is in an extraordinary situtation. Sometimes, talk shows may involve more than one guest also. The host in a talk show is a critical figure, usually someone who is a celebrity but also very eloquent and articulate. Celebrity talk shows are very popular on television. Western TV has many examples of succesful talk shows like The Oprah Winfrey Show, The Ellen DeGeneres Show, Jimmy Kimmel Live etc. The trend started with Bollywood actor Simi Garewal's Rendezvous with Simi Garewal that featured interviews of popular celebrities from Bollywood. The show included guests' personal chit-chat with the host often getting very intense and revealing personal details about their lives. Jeena Isi Ka Naam Hai was another show that featured Bollywood celebrities and their life journey both personal and professional. It combined personal interactions of the guest with the host and testominals from friends and families. Currently, Karan Johar's Koffee with Karan is also a popular show on Indian television. The show includes fun intrecations and some competitive games between the guests where the winner takes home a coffee hamper. Amir Khan's Satyameve Jayate is an example of a talk show that deals with social issues and invites guests who have suffered some injustice in the society. Like Satyamev Jayate, many talk shows also combine live audience interactions through question and answer sessions. Aap ki Adalat hosted by Rajat Sahrma is also a sucessful example of this format.

5.0 INTRODUCTION
Health Journalism: Widespread undernourishment, malnutrition, abysmal conditions of primary health care systems and many such issues plaguing the healthcare system of our country elevates our role as health journalists. Health journalists have a duty to report on such issues ethically, accurately and with a lot of integrity. In other words, it endows us with a sense of responsibility towards the public by shining a light on healthcare issues that affect us directly or indirectly. The recent coronavirus pandemic which left thousands of people dead has ignited a debate on health reforms within the country. It has called for easy accessibility and more equitable distribution of healthcare facilities across different sections of society.
5.1 LEARNING OUTCOMES
After working through this Unit, you will be able to: * Comprehend the status of health journalism in India * Know about different issues plaguing the healthcare system in the country * Understand the challenges faced by health journalists * Gain an insight into ethical challenges while reporting on health issues in India
5.2 UNDERSTANDING HEALTH JOURNALISM

Health sector has a significant role to play in a country's progress report. Several yardsticks, which include public life expectancy, maternity & mortality rate, no. of children suffering from malnourishment, serve as significant factors in understanding how well placed a country is within the human development index. Health journalists must understand the bearings of such issues within a country's health framework. They should be able to decipher scientific content and de- jargonize complex scientific terms for their general audience. Journalists covering the health sector must stay informed about new developments taking place in the field of health around the world. From latest discovery of vaccines to cutting edge scientific research, health journalism is a field which is continuously evolving and growing. Hence, health journalists have a responsibility to report accurately and effectively. They must realize that they have the power to shape public opinion and influence policymakers. Hence sensitive information should be relayed with caution, keeping in mind the consequences and far-reaching impact that such stories can have on their audience.
5.3 DISSEMINATION OF HEALTH NEWS
Mass media plays a crucial role in disseminating information. People often rely on mass media to garner information on issues related to health, such as personal hygiene, communicable and non- communicable diseases, health policies and so on. For example---A doctor's interview on impact of certain food on body systems can influence lifestyle changes among readers. In the age of the Internet, dissemination of information is rather quick. It can be done through print, TV, radio, or social media. This ready and quick availability of information also presents us with challenges. An overload of information makes it difficult for readers to sift through vast trove of information and differentiate between fake & genuine news. An example of this was clearly visible during the pandemic where misinformation was abundant, compelling reliable sources (government and genuine news media organizations) to intervene and relay accurate information from time to time to avoid panic among public.
5.4 UNDERSTANDING ETHICS OF HEALTH JOURNALISM
Accuracy and sticking to the facts remain the cornerstone of good journalism. In the age of TRPs and revenue driven model that most news organizations are grappling with, speed and breaking news syndrome have taken a toll on accuracy and objectivity. Hence, there needs to be a revival of journalism ethics. Most importantly, journalists should be mindful of scaremongering and sensationalism when it comes to health journalism. Sensationalism not only causes cultural corruption, but it can also sabotage effective measures employed by organizations to combat a situation. The pandemic was a clear example of how scaremongering and unfiltered information pouring in through social media caused panic among people. Given the context of the story, it is very important that the identity of people who are part of case studies be protected and secured. Sensitive information should not be made public. Avoid identifying people based on religion or caste as this can lead to stereotyping. Additionally, always seek the opinion of health experts who can shed light on issues precisely and accurately.
5.5 ETHICS OF INTERVIEWING
Developing and cultivating sources are significant to journalistic endeavour. One should always check the credibility of their sources. In other words, journalists should check if the sources are knowledgeable enough to give their views on a topic. Insist that your source must go on record while you are interviewing them. It can get quite dicey if your sources insist that they should be anonymous. In letting yourself quote anonymous sources there is always a possibility that your sources could go back on what they have said, and your news organization could be forced to retract the story. So, cultivate sources carefully and as much as possible avoid quoting anonymous sources. In case a source has tipped you off on a story or a happening, it is important for you as a journalist to protect the identity of the source under every circumstance. One should never compromise on that front.

5.6 CULTIVATING SOURCES
Networking is a significant way to cultivate sources. Meet your source in person and try to be in touch with them even when you are not chasing a story. The relationship between you and your sources should be more than just give and take. As a journalist it is important that you should never lie to your sources. It is paramount to keep the intent of the story clear. And most importantly, quote your sources accurately. Never twist their words. Always quote them verbatim. This is significant to gain their trust. Also, this will make it easier for you as a journalist to approach your sources next time for your story. Also, once the story is published it is important to inform your sources that they have been quoted. From time to time, it is significant to check on them. This is significant for networking purpose. Relationship between journalists and their sources should be sheerly based on trust. No other mode of transaction (money, gifts, etc) should be involved.
5.7 HANDLING SENSITIVE INFORMATION
A journalist should assess risks associated with a story. Accordingly, precautions must be taken. In the digital age this could be protecting information obtained from a source that you have tucked away in your computer. It is important to ensure that this information should be protected. According to Committee to Protect Journalists, "Protecting confidential sources is a cornerstone of ethical reporting. When journalists have agreed to protect someone's identity, they should make every effort to do so, especially in circumstances where a source could be arrested or harmed." Different ways to do that could include taking precautionary measures which involve digital safety best practices. This could be done by employing layers of security by building strong passphrase or using two-factor authentication (2FA). It is important to remove browser history and regularly update your devices. Using encryption during chats is another way to secure information. Additionally, it is important to make sure that the source you are talking to is authenticate and has information that could be valuable to you. A classic example of this could be studied through whistleblower Edward Snowden and how he passed on sensitive information to journalists which finally blew the lid on NSA's mass surveillance program.
5.8 REPORTING THE PANDEMIC
Media as a fourth pillar of democracy has an important role in bringing about change in society. It is also endowed with responsibility of bringing about positive changes within society and shed light on issues. During the pandemic, media became the source of information for most people. The government had used media to broadcast timely information on the pandemic. During the lockdown period media organizations served as the most reliable source of information for public. News media organizations also had to grapple with initial stages of reporting about coronavirus when there was clearly lack of knowledge or information about coronavirus, its nature, mode of transmission etc. During an epidemic messaging plays a very important role. We saw that from time-to-time. Clear messages were being reinforced by both the government as well as various media organizations. Mass media played a huge role in keeping people informed about the surge in covid cases. People were asked to wear masks and maintain social distancing. In a paper titled, "Making waves in India: Media and the COVID-19 pandemic," the authors argue that it becomes "imperative for the media and the government to repeatedly, perhaps in a novel manner, convey messages to the public regarding NPIs to the public to lessen the impact of the disease, primarily when the prevalence of the disease is in a downward trend." Please note, NPI here means non-pharmaceutical interventions (NPIs) which include physical distance, hand hygiene, wearing a mask, etc. to limit the spread of the disease. The paper which was published in Brookings Institution goes on to emphasize that the role of media becomes more important during a pandemic. "This did not happen on the eve of the second

wave, and the lack of relevant information likely intensified the disastrous impact of the wave," the authors say. Check Your Progress: 1 Note: 1) Write your answer in about 50 words.
